post.description:
Drives the agent's machine to the requested agent version over
the signed tunnel (the survivor-pattern update handoff). The
target version must exact-match a version on the signed
artifact rail; when the body omits target_version the org's
pinned version is the target, and an org with no pin refuses
with 422 (no unpinned-latest fallback exists on the update
path). Refusals: 404 when the agent is not in the CALLER'S
org (the ownership law — the id alone is never enough); 422
for a v1/null-version agent (manual reinstall required — its
binary predates the signature gate), a malformed/off-rail
target, or a machine that RAN the handoff script and refused
it (code manual_reinstall_required with the attempt_id — the
install does not run as root with systemd; only a reinstall
with the systemd installer fixes it); 409 for a terminal-
status (revoked/terminated/uninstalled) or key-rotation-
pending agent, an in-flight lifecycle op, or a machine with
no dispatch route; 503 when the signed rail is unavailable
(fail closed). Success is 202: the handoff is accepted and
the final outcome (confirmed / failed / restored / no-confirm)
lands in the org's audit trail as the machine reports it.
post.summary: Update an agent to a target version (org-scoped manual path)

Step 1 of the two-step confirmation (epic #3964 story C10):
the detected change (old address → new address), the
affected hostnames (the platform's edge hostnames whose
publish address matched the old address, plus the platform's
recorded route hosts — each proven by what its public DNS
answers), grouped per DNS zone with the custody verdict:
"ours" (BMC holds the zone's API custody — the execute arm
repoints and verifies) or "theirs" (the user's own DNS —
the execute arm hands over the exact record list). A
fingerprint rides the response; the execute request carries
it back, and a stale fingerprint refuses with the fresh
impact.

post.description:
Step 2 of the two-step confirmation (epic #3964 story C10):
the body carries the fingerprint of the impact the user
confirmed. For zones under BMC's custody every affected
record is re-read live immediately before its write (a
record that drifted since the confirmation is skipped with
a named outcome, never written) and repointed to the new
address; for the user's own zones nothing is written — the
exact record list (host, type, old → new) rides the answer
and the surface stays in its waiting state until the
re-check sees the names answer the new address. A stale
fingerprint (the address changed again, the records moved)
refuses with 409 consequence_changed carrying the fresh
impact — the same fail-closed shape as the delete
preflights.
post.summary: Confirm the machine's address change and act per custody

get.description:
The waiting surface's re-check (epic #3964 story C10): the
affected hostnames' public DNS is resolved and each record
reports whether it now answers the new address. When every
name answers it — ours repointed and propagated, or the
user's own change landed — the change resolves. This is the
endpoint the surface polls/refreshes; it never fakes
success: until the names answer, the state stays as it is.

provider.description:
Provider names the custody's provider ("platform" for the seat, the
registry row's provider otherwise; "" for theirs).

zone.description:
Zone is the zone's FQDN. The platform seat's zone names the edge
records; a registered row names its own.

api_healthy.description:
APIHealthy is the read-only API-liveness proof (every non-agent-role
RUNNING install — review M1): `k3s kubectl get --raw=/readyz` with a
short in-kubectl timeout. false = not proven (agent role has no local
API to ask, or the API did not answer).

node_token_hash.description:
NodeTokenHash is the SHA256 hex of the k3s server join token
(/var/lib/rancher/k3s/server/node-token) — the cluster-identity
fingerprint the adopt decision's one-cluster rule compares. The HASH
only: the raw token never crosses the wire. "" when the file is
absent. A token that exists but cannot be fingerprinted (unreadable,
sha256sum missing) FAILS the whole probe (non-zero exit → the caller's
fail-closed probe_unavailable path) — it must never read as an empty
fingerprint that vacuously "agrees" with another member's.

role.description:
Role classifies the install: RoleServer or RoleAgent; "" when no data
dir was seen (the unit + pgrep evidence still speak).

unit.description:
Unit is the systemd unit found ACTIVE: "k3s.service" (server) or
"k3s-agent.service" (worker). "" when nothing is active or the guest is
systemd-less (the pgrep fallback cannot name a unit).

blueprint.description:
Blueprint is the per-stack capability flag: this install is a
blueprint deployment, so the stack view may offer Update.

checked_at.description: CheckedAt is when the served result was checked.

commits_ahead.description: CommitsAhead is the compare count (best-effort; 0 = absent).

compare_url.description: CompareURL is the upstream commit-compare link (context).

degraded.description:
Degraded marks a check that could not run (quota spent, provider
error): NO hint — never an error to the view.

degraded_reason.description:
DegradedReason names WHY a degraded check could not run (issue
#3775): credential_unresolved (the source-pull credential cannot
mint — a revoked/suspended GitHub App installation), probe_failed
(a transient provider/probe failure), or quota (the shared budget
refused). Empty when not degraded. ADDITIVE: consumers that read
state/degraded only are unchanged.

digest_drift.description:
DigestDrift carries the tag-level movements (the digest-moved
state's rows; attached to ref-moved too).

dismissed.description:
Dismissed marks THIS instance as dismissed by its owner (the FE
renders nothing; the state survives until a new upstream SHA
range).

installed_sha.description:
InstalledSHA / UpstreamSHA are the movement's two ends (UpstreamSHA
empty on a ref that no longer resolves).

key.description:
Key is THIS instance's dismissal key (the upstream SHA range, or
the state key) — the FE's dismiss call echoes it back.

slot_drift.description:
SlotDrift carries the managed-slot declaration movements (the
managed-xyz story 7 AC1 half): the repo file's slot declaration is
the baseline, and a changed floor or engine names its rows here.
A bound-version move that satisfies the floor never lands here —
R4: the floor is a minimum, satisfying it is not drift.

state.description:
State is the named state. "none" (and "none" + Degraded) renders
NO hint — the FE renders nothing either way.

changed.description:
Changed is false when the recompile is artifact-identical — the
honest "nothing changed" answer (the FE renders it, and the apply
action offers nothing to confirm).

compare_url.description: CompareURL is the upstream commit-compare link (context).

diff.description:
Diff is the compiled-artifact diff (image digests, field set,
resources, component set).

gates.description:
Gates are the next compile's deploy-gate refusals (the card's gate
codes — the FE renders them in wizard language beside the diff; a
gated compile also refuses at apply).

next_name.description: NextName is the compiled stack name (the apply target's ref name).

source.description:
Source echoes the selection this review re-resolved (the
originally selected source — never silently switched).

changed.description: Changed is the one-flag summary: any row anywhere flips it.

components.description:
Components are the component-SET changes: services the next compile
adds or removes (the component-set law's preview half — the apply
path refuses what the law refuses; the diff shows what WOULD
change).

fields.description:
Fields are the form-field set changes (the fields: translation —
added, removed, or changed rows).

images.description:
Images are the changed image pins: per service, the compiled image
reference as each side pins it (name@sha256:… post-pin; a build
service compiles imageless on both sides and produces no row).

resources.description: Resources are the changed compute limits (cpu / memory per service).

exit_code.description:
ExitCode is the ledger's exit fact when the output ref carries
one ("exit=N"); nil when the failure landed without one.

lines.description:
Lines are the real failing lines — the attempt's last lines,
verbatim (the log store's order).

output_ref.description: OutputRef is the ledger's stored output fact, verbatim.

saw.description: Saw / Likely / ToTry are the read-only diagnosis rows.

step.description:
Step is the failing plan step (the last step the builder's
plan-echo attributed a line to); "" when no line carries an
attribution.

log_status.description:
LogStatus is "starting" until the first line lands (A28), then
"streaming" while the attempt is live; a TERMINAL attempt says so
per the ledger fact — "complete" (succeeded) or "failed" — a
finished build's pane never reads as still-streaming. LogCursor
is the tail page's last seq — the cursor the console's next
Since poll passes (the page contract, not a MAX read).

state.description:
State is the ledger's own state for the attempt (submitting /
dispatched / lost / succeeded / failed) — proven, never mapped.

ask.description:
Ask is the attach-or-connect state (the creds-invalid class's
single CTA; the retryable classes' CTA is the retry).

code.description: Code is one of the publish chain's Refuse* constants, verbatim.

registry.description: Registry names the registry the refusal came from.

retryable.description:
Retryable is the refusal's A20 class (creds-invalid never
retries — the first-class state; the other two re-check).

duration_ms.description:
DurationMs is the measured wall-clock of the whole rollback
(re-point + probe(s)) on the Gate's clock; WithinBudget is the
≤30 s budget's honest comparison.

gate.description:
Gate is the run's terminal row (proven / blocked / failed) — the
timeline's health fact for the re-entered probe gate.

routed.description:
Routed / Blocked mirror the gate verdict (traffic routes on N-1,
or the probe failed and nothing routes).

target.description: Target is the revision the service re-pointed at.

run_reference.description:
RunReference is the service's build run (the attempt ledger's
stable run identity). Empty is legal — a service whose build has
not been dispatched yet renders every stage pending.

proposed.description:
Proposed is what the replay will set unless the review overrides —
the platform default: mode off.

source.description:
Source is the source install's durability policy, as stored —
reference only, never copied into the proposal.

approved_value.description:
ApprovedValue is the review's approved target value (approved items
only).

key.description: Key is "install.key" (a stack component's is its own install).

source_value.description: SourceValue is the source-side resolved value, as the plan carries it.

detail.description:
Detail is the human-readable fact (source value beside the approved
target value for env_local items, the honest replay-empty wording).

install.description: Install is the item's install name (a stack unit's is its parent).

kind.description:
Kind is the exception kind: excluded | env-local | endpoint |
replay-empty | undeclared-class.

bundle.description:
Bundle is the chosen revision's digest-pinned bundle ref (AC 2) —
the replay Builds from THIS ref, never a re-resolved catalog entry.
Nil when the unit has no replay revision.

data_class.description:
DataClass is the install component's declared data class (AC 2) —
what decides the replay's data behavior (stateless redeploys,
stateful-derivable deploys fresh, stateful-authoritative bootstraps
empty; OPERATIONS.md:255). DataClassUndeclared when the frozen
state carries no declaration. A loose unit carries its single
component's class; a stack unit's parent record carries none (the
components carry theirs).

display_name.description:
DisplayName / PhysicalName are the record's display/physical-name
facts, carried AS STORED (AC 2). A restore-diverged source's
PhysicalName diverges from its InstallName permanently (the alias
law) — the plan shows the divergence; story 134.3's identity law
gives the CLONE a fresh PhysicalName and never copies this one.

durability.description:
Durability is the durability plan (AC 6, RULED 2026-09-27):
durability does NOT travel — the proposal is the platform default
(off) and the source's policy rides as reference; the review may
override per install.

hooks_declared.description:
HooksDeclared are the install's DECLARED seed/sanitize hooks (AC 2;
the bundle format's hook surface — bundle-declared per
OPERATIONS.md:257). Empty today: the frozen bundle format declares
no seed/sanitize hooks yet, and the plan says so rather than
guessing one.

params.description:
Params are the chosen revision's non-sensitive resolved params
(AC 2), each with its portability classification (the Param
vocabulary). Credential-class params are listed by key with their
values stripped (AC 3).

ref.description: Ref is the source install's identity (project/cluster/install).

replay.description: Replay records how the revision was chosen (ReplaySource).

replay_empty.description:
ReplayEmpty is the review-facing fact 134.2 replays by: a
stateful-authoritative install with NO declared seed hook replays
EMPTY, and the plan review says so — never a guess.

replay_revision.description:
ReplayRevision is the proposed replayed revision number: the
record's StableRevision, falling back to Current when no stable
pointer exists (RULED 2026-09-27). Zero with Replay none.

key.description: Key is the param's canonical key (the frozen ClassifyParam grammar).

portability.description: Portability is the plan's classification (the Param* vocabulary).

proposed_value.description:
ProposedValue is the env_local param's proposed target value. Nil at
derivation: nothing has resolved target facts yet — the review (or
the target resolution it approves) fills it, and the replay renders
the approved value.

source_value.description:
SourceValue is the env_local param's source-side resolved value —
shown beside the proposed target value (AC 5).

undeclared.description:
Undeclared flags the "no declaration exists" case (AC 5): the param
replays verbatim and is flagged as such — the records-predating-the-
portability-classes law. Nothing is guessed: an omitted class is a
fact, not an implied portable.

value.description:
Value is the param's resolved value — NON-sensitive by the
revision-params law. Secret-class params NEVER carry one (the field
stays empty; the value re-escrows on the target).

created_at.description:
CreatedAt / UpdatedAt are the derivation stamps (store-owned on
persistence).

endpoints.description:
Endpoints are the source scope's linked-external endpoint
registrations as target re-resolution items: name, type, host, and
port ONLY (AC 4). The registry's sealed credentials have no field
to ride — the store's reference read never selects them.

id.description:
ID is the plan's stable id (names-free; minted at derivation when the
request did not pin one).

schema_version.description: SchemaVersion is the document's schema version (PlanSchemaV1).

source_state_digest.description:
SourceStateDigest pins the derivation's inputs (the doc comment's one
sentence on the package): the source records' generations, the
StackDAGStore captures, and the external-endpoint registrations.
CheckFresh refuses execution against a source whose digest changed.

units.description:
Units are the plan's install units in source install-name order —
one per loose install, one per stack-shaped install (whose
components fold INTO the stack unit and never appear as loose
units, AC 9).

durability.description:
Durability are the per-install durability overrides (story C, issue
#4277): the clone proposes off; an override replaces the proposal,
and an override onto a destination another install writes refuses
(CheckDurabilityOverrides — the two-writer guard).

endpoints.description:
Endpoints are the linked-external re-resolution approvals: the
binding-used endpoint names the operator approved for re-resolution
against the target's registrations.

env_local.description:
EnvLocal are the env_local approvals (install + param key → the
approved target value).

excluded.description:
Excluded lists the plan units (by install name — a stack unit's name
is its PARENT install) the review excludes from the clone. Every
unit not named is accepted.

component.description: Component is the stack manifest's component name.

facts.description:
Facts are the component install's facts (its own record, revision,
bundle, params, data class, durability).

position.description:
Position is the component's index in the manifest's canonical order
(the capture's deploy-order tiebreak).

components.description:
Components are the stack's components in manifest (deploy) order —
each with its own install facts (the component installs are the
stack's durable truth; the parent record stays revision-less).

stack.description: Stack is the stack manifest's name (the capture's).

wiring.description:
Wiring is the captured wiring edges as reference items: consumer,
slot, provider, kind, and the wiring secret's NAME. Keys carries the
edge's reference values (host, port) — never a secret value (the
capture's own law).

endpoints_approved.description:
EndpointsApproved / EndpointsPending name the binding-used
link-external endpoints.

env_local_approved.description:
EnvLocalApproved / EnvLocalPending are the env_local decision items.
The approved ones carry the value beside the source value — the
confirmation view of what the replay will render; the pending ones
are the exceptions' company (they also appear in Exceptions).

state.description:
State is the plan's own state (planned | nothing-to-clone), echoed
so a caller renders the empty plan honestly.

facts.description: Facts are the unit's install facts (identity + replay plan).

slot_notes.description:
SlotNotes carries the disclosure lines the derive rendered for this
unit's managed slots (managed-xyz story A, issue #4275's wire delta:
backward-compatible JSON — omitempty, no schema bump). The interim
line states the working-but-empty posture ("database provisions
fresh at the target; starts empty — data copy follows in the seed
story") on the database class and the blast-radius line on the cache
class ("sessions, counters, queues are not copied — they start
empty"). Story B retracts the interim line when the seed lands;
story C adds the durability line.

stack.description:
Stack is non-nil exactly when the source install is stack-shaped
(a StackDAGStore capture exists for it).

keys.description: Keys are the edge's reference values (host, port), as captured.

endpoint_resolutions.description:
EndpointResolutions are the linked-external resolutions applied: the
binding's endpoint name resolved against the target's registration.

env_local_resolutions.description:
EnvLocalResolutions are the env_local resolutions the review
approved, as rendered (install.key = value).

excluded.description:
Excluded names the plan units the review excluded (story 134.4) —
what the review left out is part of the run's truth.

failures.description:
Failures name every failing install/component — a failed run's
report is the operator's first read.

gate.description: Gate is the post-clone gate's record (nil until the gate ran).

ordering_basis.description:
OrderingBasis states the replay's ordering (the honest version —
see OrderingBasis).

runbook.description:
Runbook is the recovery runbook (RunbookText) — both recovery paths
written into the report's doc.

source_project_id.description: Source / Target name the clone's two scopes.

state.description: State is the report's state (the ReportState vocabulary).

units.description:
Units are the per-install outcomes (stack components ride their own
lines — the component records ARE the stack's durable truth).

agent_heartbeat.description: AgentHeartbeat: the BMC agent's heartbeat is fresh (or the failure).

deployments_available.description:
DeploymentsAvailable: every deployment across the cloned installs'
namespaces carries the Available condition (or the failure naming
the unavailable ones).

no_pending_pvcs.description:
NoPendingPVCs: no PersistentVolumeClaim sits in Pending (or the
failure naming them).

nodes_ready.description:
NodesReady: every cluster node reports Ready ("ok (3/3 nodes Ready)"
or the failure naming the NotReady nodes).

pv_node_affinity.description:
PVNodeAffinity is N/A for a without-data clone — no PVs travel. The
check is marked, never omitted.

webhooks_resolve.description:
WebhooksResolve is N/A for a without-data clone — webhooks re-install
behind their own probe gates. Marked, never omitted.

component.description: Component names the stack component (kind stack only).

data_class.description:
DataClass is the unit's declared data class (the plan's), shown so
the report states how the data classes decided the replay.

err.description: Err carries the failing unit's refusal/failure text (failed lines).

install.description: Install is the target install's name.

kind.description: Kind is the unit kind: stack component or loose install.

provenance.description:
Provenance is the stamped provenance: cloned for every deployed
unit (the 134.3 law).

replay_empty.description:
ReplayEmpty marks the stateful-authoritative-with-no-seed-hook case:
the unit replayed EMPTY, and the report says so — never a guess.

revision.description: Revision is the revision the unit's deploy minted (deployed lines).

slot_notes.description:
SlotNotes carries the interim disclosure lines the derive rendered
for the owning unit's managed slots (managed-xyz story A, issue
#4275's wire delta: backward-compatible JSON). The settled report
states the working-but-empty posture beside the outcome. Story B
retracts the line when the seed lands; story C adds the durability
line.

stack.description: Stack names the owning stack (kind stack only).

cpu_millicores.description: integer millicores — no floats on the canonical wire

slice.description: the slice identity on the machine

foreign_target.description:
ForeignTarget shows the existing record's target when State ==
taken (the R6 refusal's "the existing target shown" courtesy).

migration_eligible.description:
MigrationEligible reports, when State == ours, whether the tag's
cluster id names a LIVE cluster row of THIS org (issue #2713 — the
record-migration flow's green light: only then can an org admin
record a migration consent for the host). Strictly read-only: a
failed lookup answers false and never fails the availability
answer (the honest degrade — eligible=false is exactly what the
consent surface would refuse on).

ours.description:
Ours carries the ownership identity when State == ours (the tag's
cluster and arrival — the same grammar the executor composes).

state.description:
State: available (no record), ours (a BMC-tagged record), or taken
(a foreign record). The R6 law's read-only face.

advisories.description:
Advisories carries the C11 nesting heads-ups ("zone X nests inside
registered zone Y").

ns_warnings.description:
NSWarnings lists the zones whose C3 advisory fired (a warning at
connect — the registry still records them; the preflight hardens).

check.description:
Check names the rung ("token", "zone-read", "dns-edit" — or the
arrival checklist's "account", "tunnel-scope").

ok.description: OK reports whether the rung passed.

nested_under.description:
NestedUnder / Contains name already-registered zones this zone
nests with (the C11 advisory: one heads-up, never a refusal).

ns_mismatch.description:
NSMismatch reports the C3 advisory: the internet's delegation does
not (yet) point at the provider's declared nameservers — a WARNING
at connect (a user may be mid-migration), a refusal at preflight.

branch.description:
Branch + CommitSHA name the ref the push carried (the mover's
update-ref input — a bare packfile carries no refs).

fetch_path.description:
FetchPath is the pack's fetch path relative to the edge base URL
the sidecar's env carries (the Bearer redemption URL).

fetch_token.description:
FetchToken is the 12-char Base32 PLAINTEXT fetch credential (the
registration-token mint's #1511 law: shown once, hash-only at rest).
Single-use, 15-minute TTL, bound to (org, project, repo, push).

pack_digest.description:
PackDigest is the stored pack's sha256 (hex) — the sidecar verifies
what it fetched against it before landing the pack in Forgejo.

family.description: Family / TopK / Cadence echo a metric declaration's contract.

presentation.description:
Presentation echoes the spec's rendering hint (the per-kind default
when the spec left it empty).

reason.description: Reason carries the degraded/unavailable cause. Empty otherwise.

rows.description: Rows carries the exec collector's stdout lines (the table fact).

state.description: State is the honest rendering vocabulary (the constants above).

apply_time_allowance.description: ApplyAllowance is the backend's apply-time allowance ("2m").

budget.description: Budget is the workflow activity budget ("45m").

health.description:
Health is the arrival's health (the frozen ArrivalHealth
vocabulary). Health is defined per shape: a SaaS connector arrival
reports its connector deployment's ready replicas equal to desired;
an API-less arrival reports a reachability probe of its far end.

instance.description:
Instance is the arrival addon instance id (matches the route
binding's ingress.instance).

kind.description:
Kind is the arrival family (the bundle.ArrivalKind vocabulary — one
vocabulary across the route binding and the facts).

provider.description:
Provider names the arrival provider behind the instance (story
154.6 — the compile's shape stamp reads it: the step sequence, the
reservation slot, and the co-tenant plan warning are per-provider
declarations, and the facts are where the LIVE provider is named).
Additive omitempty: pre-154.6 facts marshal and parse unchanged, and
the compile treats a missing provider as the remote-config posture
(cloudflare's landed behavior) — never a guess.

publish_address.description:
PublishAddress is the address traffic arrives at: the gateway's
publish address for public; the full arrival target for a tunnel
(the tunnel CNAME for cloudflare — including the tunnel id, never a
domain suffix). The compile targets THIS address for a
tunnel-arrival-bound route, never the gateway publish.

class.description: Class is the storage class the fact describes.

eligible_node_count.description:
EligibleNodeCount is the platform's declared count of nodes eligible
for the class, as a decimal string ("3") so an UNPARSEABLE count
classifies at the consume point. ABSENT (nil) is MISSING-FACT;
negative or unparseable is MALFORMED-FACT; a per-node fact declaring
0 is the capacity-UNSUPPORTED refusal; a system fact carrying a
NONZERO count is MALFORMED-FACT (a system fact declares 0).

nodes.description:
Nodes are the per-node free figures; a system fact lawfully carries
none. An empty or partial list (len(nodes) < eligible_node_count) is
MISSING-FACT; duplicated nodes or MORE entries than the declared
eligible count are MALFORMED-FACT. omitempty: a system fact
serializes without it.

scope.description:
Scope is the fact's scope kind (the frozen CapacityScope
vocabulary); a value outside it is MALFORMED-FACT.

system_free_bytes.description:
SystemFreeBytes is the system scope's single free figure (a quantity
string); a per-node fact MUST carry no value — the exclusivity is
MALFORMED-FACT. omitempty: a per-node fact serializes without it.

activity_budget.description:
ActivityBudget is the restore-activity budget pair (the dk64 ledger,
R7 — the member's schema is Story A's, its production and transport
the backend plumbing's): Budget is the workflow activity budget the
gate's budgeted phases price against, ApplyAllowance is the backend's
apply-time allowance for the unbudgeted seconds-scale phases. EITHER
figure absent, unparseable, negative, or zero refuses at compile (a
negative allowance under-counts the gate's budget sum). Nil on facts
collected before dk64 Story A; omitempty keeps pre-dk64 facts
byte-identical.

arch.description: Arch is the node architecture: amd64 | arm64.

arrivals.description:
Arrivals are the cluster's installed ingress arrival addons (epic
154, §4.2 — the additive growth after Gateway, following the
ClaimedHosts/Datastore precedent): one entry per arrival addon
instance, naming the arrival kind, its instance id, the address
traffic arrives at (the full tunnel CNAME for cloudflare; a
provider-native endpoint for the other shapes), and its health. The
Gateway field above stays THE PLATFORM ENTRY — arrival-aware
consumers (the plan-time binding resolution, the WAF gate, the
backend's appurls classifier) read both, never one instead of the
other. A route bound to an arrival this list does not show installed
AND healthy refuses at plan (ErrArrivalNotHealthy — intent vs
facts). omitempty keeps pre-154 facts byte-identical.

claimed_hosts.description:
ClaimedHosts are the route hostnames other installs on this cluster
already claim — the fact the hostname-uniqueness preflight (EDGE.md
§4 rule 1) checks route hosts against; a collision refuses naming the
conflicting install. The HOST keeps this registry authoritative
(record on provision, release on uninstall); omitempty keeps legacy
facts byte-identical.

class_capacities.description:
ClassCapacities are the per-class free-capacity facts the platform's
node agents assembled (the dk64 ledger, R12 — free-space facts:
`df` plus thin-pool free via lvs/vgs): per-node classes carry one
free figure per eligible node, network-backed classes one system
figure. Capacity facts reach the restore compile through this
member; ClassCapacity.Validate enforces the R12 shape at every
consume point — a malformed or missing fact refuses by name, never a
vacuous minimum. omitempty keeps pre-dk64 facts byte-identical.

data_disk_fs.description:
DataDiskFS is the host data-disk filesystem (the frozen DataDiskFS
vocabulary). Continuous FILE sync requires a CoW snapshot
layer — on plain ext4 the resolve-time check refuses it
(STORAGE.md §3).

datastore.description:
Datastore is the cluster's k3s datastore fact (story 132.5,
STORAGE.md §10.3 addition 3 — cluster facts as plan inputs): the
datastore kind (sqlite | etcd), the server members, and the
normalized server flag set. The etcd-conversion plan refuses without
it (the planner never plans on hope) and its quorum + flag-match
preflights read it. Nil on every cluster that has not recorded the
fact yet; omitempty keeps pre-132.5 facts byte-identical.

destinations.description:
Destinations are the backup destinations the platform's destination
registry offers as viable for this install (user's buckets, probed
reachable). A durability.destination outside this set is refused at
resolve (ErrCapabilityUnavailable).

domains.description: Domains are the manageable zones for env_local hostnames.

gateway.description:
Gateway is the cluster's edge-gateway publish fact (story 130.2,
EDGE.md §2) — the flavor the cluster runs and the address its edge
publishes. The web-class compile targets it instead of guessing: the
dns-apply instructions point here, dns-verify expects it, and
route-apply renders for its flavor. Nil when the cluster has no
gateway addon yet — a web compile refuses without it.
omitempty so pre-130.2 persisted facts re-marshal byte-identically.

node_tier.description:
NodeTier is the node's memory tier (the frozen NodeTier vocabulary).
The 1gb tier narrows durability to off/scheduled only (STORAGE.md §7).

provides.description:
Provides are the target context's OFFER-SIDE facts (story 135-5,
GH #2957 — the move-time re-resolution surface the v1 deferral
named): one entry per provider the target offers an incoming
binding — an install exposing a runtime context or a registered
shared endpoint — with the offered type, version, and free
capacity. The archived bindings' re-resolution (unpark/move/import)
consumes these offers: a descriptor's linked binding re-resolves
against the TARGET's offers, never the origin's records (a move
purges the origin long before the restore runs), and a declared
requires fact the offers cannot answer refuses at resolve with the
named gap — never a half-import. omitempty keeps pre-135-5 facts
byte-identical (the Arrivals pattern).

storage_class_defaults.description:
StorageClassDefaults is the cluster's default-StorageClass pair (the
dk64 ledger, R11's schema home): Observed is the class the cluster's
k8s default-storage-class annotation named at collection — the
CLUSTER-OBSERVED default — and Declared is the platform's own
declaration (empty = the platform declares nothing, and the observed
default governs). The restore compile renders the observed default
into the payload and refuses a disagreement between the two naming
both. Nil on facts collected before dk64 Story A; omitempty keeps
pre-dk64 facts byte-identical.

storage_classes.description:
StorageClasses are the storage classes the platform declared on this
cluster (STORAGE.md §7 tiering is compiled FROM these). A
storage.class value outside this set is refused at resolve
(ErrCapabilityUnavailable).

kind.description: Kind is the datastore kind (the frozen DatastoreKind vocabulary).

server_flags.description:
ServerFlags are the k3s server flags as the platform observed them,
canonicalized by NormalizeServerFlags (sorted "flag=value" pairs) —
the flag-match preflight compares the observed set against this one
and refuses drift.

servers.description:
Servers are the cluster's server (control-plane) node names — the
quorum fact the conversion preflight reads.

effective_cadence.description:
EffectiveCadence is the cadence as floored per node tier
(STORAGE.md §3); recomputed on facts revision. The RPO badge displays
THIS, never the requested one.

policy_gen.description:
PolicyGen is the separate CAS token for durability edits: inert edits
bump THIS, never Generation, so a notify-grade change must not fence
an in-flight upgrade into re-quiesce + second backup.

recovery_window.description:
RecoveryWindow is the panel-configurable PITR window (story 132.3a,
the epic-132 ruling): how far back point-in-time recovery promises,
whole days ("7d"), default DefaultRecoveryWindow. Additive field
with omitempty: policies written before 132.3a decode with it empty
and re-marshal byte-identically. Inert at the record level — the
effective bound is always the oldest surviving VERIFIED base, which
retention (the preset) keeps alive.

retention_preset.description:
RetentionPreset is one of the named presets only — free-form
per-object retention is illegal under the dependency-graph law
(STORAGE.md §6).

flavor.description:
Flavor is the gateway flavor the cluster chose ONCE (v1 vocabulary:
caddy). The choice is sticky per cluster (EDGE.md §4 rule 3) — v1
renders caddy only; a migration is a documented re-deploy.

publish_address.description:
PublishAddress is the address the gateway's edge publishes: an IP
(A-record form) or a hostname (CNAME form — tunnel topologies). The
record type the dns steps use FOLLOWS this form.

arrival_instance.description:
ArrivalInstance names the arrival addon instance serving the claimed
host (empty for the platform entry). Re-stamped with ArrivalKind.

arrival_kind.description:
ArrivalKind is the claim's arrival dimension (epic 154, §4.2): the
arrival family serving the claimed host (bundle.ArrivalKind
vocabulary). Empty on pre-154 claims — the dimension is additive
omitempty and legacy claims marshal/parse byte-identically.

The re-stamp law: the claim is re-stamped with the CURRENT
revision's arrival dimension on every route-changing revision (a
provision-time stamp goes stale the moment an app migrates arrival
on upgrade). Claims stay cluster-global — a DNS name points one
place regardless of which edge serves it — and the current-revision
dimension is what the addon-uninstall refusal and the per-arrival
teardown read. The HOST registry owns the stamping (record on
provision, release on uninstall); this fact shape is the engine's
contract for what it reads.

host.description:
Host is the claimed hostname (normalized: lowercase, no trailing
dot).

install_name.description:
InstallName names the install holding the claim — the conflicting
install a uniqueness refusal names (the backend maps that refusal to
HTTP 422; the module's contract is the sentinel).

failure_limit.description:
FailureLimit is the tolerated breach count: the gate fails when the
breaching-sample count reaches it. Zero = DefaultGateFailureLimit.

max_delta.description: MaxDelta is the LEGACY form's ± tolerance vs the baseline.

metric.description:
Metric is the LEGACY form's metric name (query's back-compat
reading).

min_samples.description:
MinSamples is the scarcity floor: fewer usable samples in the
window is INCONCLUSIVE (pause for a human), never a silent pass.
Zero = DefaultGateMinSamples.

provider.description:
Provider names a registered source ("gateway" = the gateway
counter-delta provider; story 137.1). Unknown providers are an
evaluation-time Inconclusive-with-reason, never a silent pass; the
reserved phase-2 names refuse at plan time.

query.description:
Query names the signal in the provider's grammar (the gateway
provider v1: requests | errors | error_rate | latency, optionally
"@<route>" — the backend workflow documents exactly what it
implements).

settle.description:
Settle delays evaluation from window start — warm-up samples are
skipped, never judged. Zero = evaluate from the first sample.

threshold_range.description:
ThresholdRange is the inclusive [min, max] window a sample must sit
inside. Nil + legacy fields = the ±MaxDelta reading; neither
refuses at plan time (a gate that can never decide).

free_bytes.description: FreeBytes is the node's free bytes as a quantity string.

node.description: Node is the node name the figure was measured on.

capacity_free.description:
CapacityFree maps the capacity keys to free figures (k8s resource
quantities, the ProvidesContext shape) the platform can answer for.
A declared requires capacity key this map cannot answer refuses the
binding at resolve with the named key — the facts are the offer
side's whole truth now, so an unanswered declared fact is a gap,
never a guess.

name.description:
Name is the offer's identity — the offering install's name or the
registered endpoint's name: the reference a re-link recommendation
names.

type.description:
Type is the provider type the offer serves (the BindingSlot.Type
vocabulary: postgres, redis, ...).

version.description:
Version is the offered software version when the platform can
answer for it. Empty means the offer reports no version — a slot
whose requires declares a version constraint cannot verify against
this offer, and a linked binding refuses at resolve naming the gap.

declared.description:
Declared is the platform's default-class declaration; empty =
declared nothing.

observed.description: Observed is the default class the cluster's annotation named.

allow_volume_expansion.description:
AllowVolumeExpansion is the class's allowVolumeExpansion flag as the
platform observed it on the StorageClass object (the dk64 ledger's
standing interpretation). POINTER on purpose: an omitempty plain bool
drops false on the wire, making capability-FALSE
wire-indistinguishable from UNKNOWN — nil = unknown (collected before
the flag existed, or no live read backed it), false = refused
capability, true = expandable. The restore gate's phase-0 live read
overwrites a carried nil before any consumer runs (an absent field on
the live object maps to false, never pointer-nil), so no gate phase
ever sees UNKNOWN from a live-verified path; a compile-side refusal
on nil applies only where no live read exists, and the member's
ABSENCE from the payload (not a nil flag inside a present fact) is
the MISSING-FACT case. Additive field (omitempty): facts written
before dk64 Story A decode with it nil and re-marshal
byte-identically.

replication.description:
Replication is the class's replica factor (1 | 3); replicated
classes are refused below vendor minimums (STORAGE.md §7).

snapshot_layer.description:
SnapshotLayer marks CoW snapshot capability — required for
continuous FILE sync.

cluster_id.description:
ClusterID is the engine's cluster ref (the numeric cluster row id in
string form — the re-target preview's cluster_id parameter).

dead_target.description:
DeadTarget is the plan's stamped prior target — the dead tunnel
CNAME the stranded records still point at (the condition the
re-target clears).

instance.description:
Instance is the arrival addon instance id (the preview's instance
parameter).

live_target.description:
LiveTarget is the recreated tunnel's current target (the re-target's
destination), best-effort at refusal time — empty when the live read
failed (the refusal's own message still names the tunnel).

code.description:
Code and Detail are the typed refusal (issue #4493): read back from
the stream's coded event. Empty on every other event.

superseded_at.description:
SupersededAt is when an ensure found a different live id (NULL while
the row is the ledger's active memory — during the refusal window the
active row IS the dead id, superseded only by the ensure that clears).

target.description:
Target is the full tunnel CNAME (the string a stranded record's
content equals, by the full-target equality law).

tunnel_id.description: TunnelID is the provider's opaque tunnel id whose CNAME this was.

basis.description:
Basis names the attribution: the lineage tunnel id whose target the
record points at (empty on untouched rows).

current_target.description: CurrentTarget is the record's stored content (the dead tunnel CNAME).

detail.description:
Detail carries the untouched rows' reason (the unknown-tunnel line or
the tag-mismatch line naming the interactive flow).

host.description: Host is the record's hostname, lowercased, no trailing dot.

new_target.description:
NewTarget is the live tunnel's CNAME — the write phase's destination
(empty on untouched rows: they are never written).

proxied.description:
Proxied is the record's preserved orange-cloud flag as read at the
preview (the write re-stamps proxied per the tunnel-target law, R16
C17 — a tunnel CNAME routes only orange-clouded).

record_type.description:
RecordType is the provider's record type (a stranded tunnel record is
a CNAME; only CNAMEs are judged).

tagged.description: Tagged reports whether the record carries the platform ownership tag.

zone.description: Zone is the record's zone FQDN (the registry's normalized form).

zone_id.description: ZoneID is the zone's registry row id (the report's deep link).

candidates.description: Candidates are the attributable records (outcome retarget).

cluster_id.description:
ClusterID is the triple's cluster ref (the engine's numeric cluster
row id in string form).

dead_targets.description: DeadTargets lists every remembered dead target (the attribution set).

instance.description: Instance is the arrival addon instance id.

live_target.description:
LiveTarget is the live tunnel's full CNAME — the re-target
destination every candidate would move to.

untouched.description: Untouched are the records the preview names but will never write.

zones.description:
Zones carries the zone-level outcomes (no-custody / failed) for zones
whose records could not be enumerated.

current_target.description:
CurrentTarget is the preview row's CurrentTarget — the before-state
the approval reviewed (reported in the outcome when the live record
has since moved to a different dead target).

host.description: Host is the record's hostname (the preview row's Host).

record_type.description: RecordType is the record's type (the preview row's RecordType).

zone.description: Zone is the record's zone FQDN (the preview row's Zone).

latency_ms.description:
LatencyMS is the round trip's milliseconds — the exec's dispatch,
the query, and the stream's assembly (the wire form; the handler
serializes this struct verbatim).

state.description:
State is the live registration's state, or "enabled" for an
already-enabled install (the enablement row's state).

adoptable.description:
Adoptable is the live registration/install this repo + connection
already carries (nil = none). The FE renders the adoption offer
instead of the create form.

compose_healthcheck.description:
ComposeHealthcheck reports the compose file declared a healthcheck
command — the mapping to an HTTP path is lossy, so health is still
asked (never guessed).

health_asked.description:
HealthAsked reports that the confirm step must ask for the health
path (a serving port is known). Always true for v1 detections.

ignored_expose.description:
IgnoredEXPOSE lists the Dockerfile EXPOSE ports beyond the first, in
file order — the predicate names what it ignored.

name_suffixed.description:
NameSuffixed reports the collision suffix fired (the surface says
why the name differs from the repo name).

notes.description: Notes carries the human-readable trace of the predicate's decisions.

port.description: Port is the PROPOSED serving port.

port_source.description:
PortSource names where the port came from: "compose", "expose", or
"default" (the default is a proposal the user confirms).

proposed_install_name.description:
ProposedInstallName is the DNS-1123 derivation (with the 8-hex
collision suffix when a live install already holds the base name).

shape.description:
Shape is "dockerfile" (the only v1 shape; a single-service compose
refines a Dockerfile shape, it never replaces it).

park.description:
Park is the honest-state badge (issue #2709 §2.7, additive and
omitempty): the install's active parked upgrade — a migrating CI
push holding for a panel confirm. Present on EVERY state this
section renders while the park is active; absent when nothing is
parked.

pending_expires_at.description:
PendingExpiresAt states the pending TTL (Law 13: the deadline is
stated on the surface). Set only in the pending state.

registration_rotate.description:
RegistrationRotate is the render hint for the registration-token
rotate verb (issue #2501, additive and omitempty): set true ONLY on
the enabled-registration path. It derives from the registration
row's existence and state — NEVER from an active token existing (the
dead-credential install is exactly the install that must show the
verb). A render hint only; the verb's own guards remain the
authority.

trigger_id.description:
TriggerID is the binding id (BAR-5749 row 1, additive + omitempty):
the git_build_triggers row bound to this install's repo, so the
manual deploy affordance addresses the binding directly (the deploy
route's trigger_id half). Org-scoped through the connection join
(the binding's tenancy law); absent when the repo has no binding —
the deploy control stays hidden.

added.description:
Added / Removed / Remounted name the deltas: a remount is the D1
same-name mount-path change (the claim survives, the app would boot
reading an empty directory).

current.description: Current is the deployed claim set (what the app holds now).

proposed.description: Proposed is the target's claim set (this push).

valid.description: Valid is true if Time is not NULL

ami_id.description:
Advanced options (for explicit user control)
If provided, these bypass the VM planner's decision-making

bastion_enabled.description: Story 18-7-8: SSH Security fields (Context-Based Access Control)

user_public_ips.description: Manual SSH access IPs (appended to allow list)

roles.description: vm_id -> role mapping (optional, auto-assign if omitted)

attempt_id.description:
AttemptID is the build-attempt ledger row id: the key the console and
logs reads take (/build-attempts/:attempt_id/console, /logs). Zero, and
omitted, when held (no row was written).

reason.description: held only — the ruled gate text

addons.description:
Addons is the wizard Add-ons step's checkbox set (epic app-platform
story 3.4): the optional extras ticked at formation, from the
CLOSED set models.ClusterAddons (monitoring, public_entry,
databases, log_book). The omitted/empty field records none. An
unknown key is a 400 caller error; the set is normalized again
pre-row in the service and persisted as the clusters.addons JSON
array. Installation honesty: only 'monitoring' has a real install
path today (the formation-completion hook provisions the in-cluster
monitoring stack); the other three keys persist as
declared-but-not-yet-installing — the surfaces list them, nothing
fake-installs them.

adopt_existing.description:
AdoptExisting is the EXPLICIT ADOPT opt-in (story 124.3, constraint
4): accept pre-existing, RUNNING, same-version k3s on the members
instead of installing. Without it, a member with running k3s is 409
existing_k3s_running. The server verifies EVERY member via the
contamination preflight before honoring it (verified adoption
records cluster.adopted=true; an unverified opt-in is not honored).
Mutually exclusive with ReplaceExisting (400) — adopting keeps the
user's install; replacing tears it out.

agent_deploy_method.description:
AgentDeployMethod selects how the k8s-agent is deployed inside the
cluster after provisioning: "kubectl" (default, applies manifest via
client-go) or "helm" (installs via Helm SDK from the chart repo).

backup.description:
Backup is the wizard Backup step's decision (epic app-platform
story 3.3): the plan plus, when the plan is daily/hourly, the
vault-guarded S3 connection the backups land in. Retention is
PLAN-IMPLIED and derived server-side — the client never sends it.
The omitted field (the import path, API callers that never chose)
records no decision; "none" records the explicit no-backups
choice. The org-authoritative check (connection exists, belongs
to the caller's org) lives in the service — the structured 409s
map below.

failure_policy.description:
FailurePolicy is the E5-7 LOCKED failure policy for multi-master
creates (story 125.3): "system_managed" (per-master retries to the
deadline, then the quorum-preconditioned auto-return ladder) or
"user_managed" (hold + action_required on first failure, zero
autonomous actions). Locked for the operation; persisted with the
operation record (job payload + the D6 hold) — never a cluster
column. Multi-master only; single-master ignores it.

install_config.description:
InstallConfig overrides distribution install defaults. Keys recognized by
the distribution (e.g. "snapshotter") set the corresponding flag; unknown
keys are passed through as --key=value. Empty = use distribution defaults.

network_id.description:
NetworkID is the explicit network contract (story 124.17, D12): the
network every member VM must belong to, selected in wizard step 1.
Nullable — null = the acknowledged "No network — advanced" choice
(every member must be networkless). Validated server-side against
every member; violations surface as structured 409s
(vm_not_in_network / vm_in_cluster).

replace_existing.description:
ReplaceExisting is the BAR-3685 replace confirmation (BAR-3707):
the caller accepted the ONE confirm prompt over a pre-existing
cluster — ANY version, running or stopped — so the create proceeds
with a clean-install of the requested version (the flag rides the
cluster row; formation tears the existing install out first). The
import flow never sends it (import stays best-effort, unchanged).

vm_ids.description:
VMIDs is the array of VM IDs for BYOV clusters. The first VM
is assigned the master role; all others are workers. For
explicit per-VM role assignment, use VMRoles instead.

vm_roles.description:
VMRoles allows explicit per-VM role assignment. When provided,
it overrides the implicit first-VM-is-master convention.
Each entry maps a VM ID to its role ("master" or "worker").
If omitted, VMIDs is used with the first element as master.

client_envelope.description:
ClientEnvelope is the browser-sealed stored copy of the credentials
JSON ({username, password, login_server, ca_certificate} — the keys
present in the request). Required whenever the request carries any of
those fields (issue #4424, B5): the server stores the bytes and never
encrypts. The plaintext fields still ride the request for the one live
check (registry design RC5, create half).

url.description:
URL is enforced in the handler, not here: docker-hub-public creates may
omit it (issue #3577 — the endpoint auto-fills to the Hub API URL),
while every other type still requires it.

client_envelope.description:
ClientEnvelope is the browser-sealed copy of PrivateSSHKey the server
stores (issue #4424, B7); the plaintext is used for the availability
probe only and never persisted.

ip_address.description: Remote connection details (required only if IsLocal is false)

is_local.description: true for local machine, false for remote

purpose.description:
Purpose + DraftName carry the durable cluster-create draft intent
(story 124.17 AC7). The wizard sends purpose="cluster-create" plus the
cluster name it is heading toward; ordinary network creates omit both.
Only "cluster-create" is accepted today — anything else is stripped so
the column cannot be used as a free-text channel.

service_account_json.description:
ServiceAccountJSON is the gcs native credential (issue #3879): the
plaintext JSON key for a service account, replacing the HMAC pair.

account.description:
azblob (Azure Blob) fields — issue #3576. Account is the storage
account (the endpoint synthesizes from it), Container the blob
container, and AccessKey the storage key (key mode).

LinkedCredentialID is link mode for EVERY provider (issue #3874): the
connection borrows an org cloud credential and must carry no raw keys.
Accepted pairs: aws/minio/wasabi/other link an aws credential, gcs links
a gcp credential, azblob links an azure credential.

ServiceAccountJSON is the gcs native credential (issue #3879): paste the
JSON key Google Cloud issues for a service account. It replaces the
HMAC pair on new GCS connections; region still records the location and
an endpoint may be omitted.

client_envelope.description:
ClientEnvelope is the browser-sealed copy of PrivateSSHKey the server
stores (issue #4424, B8); the plaintext is for the live probe only.

bastion_enabled.description: Story 18-7-8: SSH Security fields (Context-Based Access Control)

user_public_ips.description: Manual SSH access IPs (appended to allow list)

supersede_revoke.description:
SupersedeRevoke is the browser-minted revoke token for the machine's
PREVIOUS mandate (review should-fix 3): a re-mint flips the backend
row to superseded, but the machine keeps the predecessor certificate
INSTALLED until a revoke push names it — without the token, a stale
installed mandate plus a replayed unconsumed action signature could
resurrect narrowed-away authority. Required whenever this mint
supersedes a live predecessor; the nonce must name THAT mandate.

acknowledge_irreversible.description:
AcknowledgeIrreversible is the AC5 confirm-again flag (the server's
irreversibility_warning 409 carries the verbatim text; re-submit with
this true).

impact_fingerprint.description:
ImpactFingerprint is the epic-#3964 story-C1 execute-time
re-verification handle: the fingerprint GET /clusters/:id/delete-impact
returned. When provided and the consequences moved since that preflight,
the delete refuses with 409 consequence_changed carrying the fresh
impact. Absent = the legacy contract, unchanged.

egress_allowlist.description:
EgressAllowlist is OPTIONAL (the 2026-10-08 drill composition):
the hostname-suffix list the dispatched job's egress guard allows.
Absent/empty composes the deny-all default (fail closed); the
entry grammar is the contracts battery's egress_suffix law,
enforced at dispatch — the one law, never a bind-time second copy.

vault_envelope.description:
The sealed-delivery bind (issue #4328, design SD5; refined AC 6):
the browser generated the HMAC secret locally and sealed BOTH blobs
before upload — the vault row under the org vault key (the #4025
envelope, base64 over [nonce][ciphertext+tag] per blob) and the
machine box (the anonymous sealed box, base64 over the wire framing)
addressed to the verifying machine's delivery public key. The server
stores both verbatim; plaintext never rides this wire in either
direction.

verifying_agent_id.description:
VerifyingAgentID is the connection's ONE designated verifying
machine (SD5's v1 designation rule).

rotate_new_pubkey.description:
The RotateGuardKey payload (rotation class only): the new guard PUBLIC
key (base64-std) and the dual-key window's end (unix seconds). Stored
verbatim; the agent verifies and applies.

signature.description:
Signature is base64-std of the raw Ed25519 signature over the
canonical token encoding (the browser's wire form; stored verbatim).

signer_user_id.description:
Signer attribution (#4036, per-user minting keys): the minting user's
id and guard-key fingerprint (base64url SHA-256 of the pubkey). The
backend CANNOT verify the claim (it holds no guard key) — it records
what the authenticated session minted, and the AGENT's roster verifies
the signature itself.

adopt_ingress.description:
AdoptIngress is the explicit consent flag (story 133.3, GH #2200 AC
2, optional): when the target cluster runs a live traefik holding
ingress, importing requires the owner's explicit acceptance that the
platform's caddy gateway addon takes ingress over (traefik stops
serving it). Without the flag a traefik-holding cluster REFUSES the
import with named, guided alternatives — never a silent ingress
takeover. Honorable only while the adoption is lossless (traefik
serves no Traefik-native CRD routes the addon cannot replace).

cluster_id.description:
ClusterID is present on the auto-install path (kubeconfig provided).
The FE uses it to navigate to the cluster detail page and subscribe
to progress events. Nil on the manual path (no cluster row yet).

vm_name.description: For VM installations (only valid with bare-metal/imported)

expiration_mode.description:
ExpirationMode + DurationMinutes carry the maintainer's dual-mode choice
(Epic 103 / ADR-078). ExpirationMode is "fixed" (default) or "sliding".
DurationMinutes sets the fixed deadline or the initial sliding window;
it defaults to 15 when unset or out of range.

remaining_backup_codes.description: Number of unused backup codes left

qr_code_url.description: otpauth://totp/... (put in an on the frontend)

operation.description:
Operation is one of the reviewed spender slugs (the vaultrental
allowlist — an unknown operation is a 400).

payload.description: Payload is the released secret material (the browser's local decrypt).

target_ref.description:
TargetRef names what the operation spends ("<type>:<id>" by
convention) — the correlation key the spender handler consumes on.

ttl_minutes.description:
TTLMinutes is optional; 0/absent = the 15-minute default, values
beyond the 60-minute ceiling are refused (never clamped).

account.description: Issue #3576 — azblob fields (empty for the S3-family providers).

credentials.description:
Credentials is ALWAYS a masked view. The list path does not even decrypt
(AC5); the create/edit paths return this same minimal placeholder.

has_vault_credentials.description:
HasVaultCredentials tells the FE whether a "rotate" affordance applies
(104.4). It does NOT leak the secret.

last_verified_at.description:
LastVerifiedAt is RFC3339 (UTC) or "" when the connection has never
passed a check (BAR-5678). Populated by the LIST path from one bulk
read of the verification ledger; the create/update/rotate responses
carry "" (the zero value) — the same law as the project scope.

linked_credential_id.description:
LinkedCredentialID is set on link-mode rows of every provider (issue
#3874; azblob since #3576): the connection authenticates through that
org cloud credential and stores no vault credentials of its own, so a
key rotation does not apply to it.

region.description: Region is the S3-family region (issue #3874); empty for azblob rows.

truncated.description:
Truncated is true when more rows existed inside the window than the
read's row cap served — the card renders a "showing the newest N"
note instead of truncating silently (review should-fix 4).

recovery_key_created_at.description: RecoveryKeyCreatedAt is when the CURRENT recovery key was generated.

recovery_key_fingerprint.description:
RecoveryKeyFingerprint is base64url(SHA-256(recovery key)) — A9
metadata: proof a key exists, never the key.

cluster_id.description:
ClusterID is the Platform the machine's VM belongs to. Omitted when the
VM is in no Platform (unassigned) or there is no VM row. Never null.

fingerprint.description:
Fingerprint is "sha256:<hex>" of the enrolled Ed25519 public key — a
hash, never key material. Empty for legacy agents enrolled before
ADR-065 Phase 2 (rendered honestly as "no enrolled key").

last_delivery_at.description:
LastDeliveryAt is the newest ledger row for this machine (nil when
the ledger has nothing for it — an honest "never", not a fabricated
date).

vm_id.description:
VMID is the machine's VM row id (BAR-1588 / BAR-1600). Omitted when the
agent has no VM row (a kubernetes or imported enrollment).

acknowledged.description:
Acknowledged is the A9 gate: the replace dialog's "I stored this key"
checkbox. The endpoint refuses to invalidate the old key until the
browser says the user stored the new one.

recovery_key_fingerprint.description:
RecoveryKeyFingerprint is base64url(SHA-256(new recovery key)) —
computed in the browser; the server records it, never the key.

recovery_salt.description:
RecoverySalt is the fresh 32-byte Argon2id salt for the new
recovery derivation (browser-generated, public by construction).

recovery_slot.description:
RecoverySlot is the new recovery-wrapped vault key (opaque,
components/vault/slots format, wrapped under
Argon2id(new recovery key, RecoverySalt) in the browser).

new_vault_salt.description:
Client-wrapped new password slot (base64) + its fresh Argon2id salt
(base64, 32 bytes) + the new password — the #4026 browser flow's
artifacts. All-or-nothing: any subset is a 400. The slot is an
opaque blob the server stores verbatim (the same shape
components/vault/slots wraps server-side).

client_envelope.description:
ClientEnvelope is the browser-sealed stored copy of the new
credentials JSON (issue #4424, B5) — required when the patch rotates
userpass/token credentials. The plaintext password still rides the
request for the one live check.

network_id.description:
NetworkID is the network the mesh probe measures (required for the
mesh plane; rejected for direct).

plane.description: Plane defaults to "direct"; "mesh" requires the network_id.

retest.description:
Retest is the AC-5 affordance: explicitly invalidate the cached
failed verdict and probe again (rate-limit counted).

suggested_kind.description:
SuggestedKind is the mandate class the approve should mint (#4036):
the maintenance lanes' strands suggest the renewable maintenance class.

account.description: Issue #3576 — azblob fields (empty for the S3-family providers).

credentials.description: Credentials is ALWAYS a masked view — never decrypted on this path.

has_vault_credentials.description: HasVaultCredentials tells the FE whether a "rotate" affordance applies.

last_verified_at.description:
LastVerifiedAt is RFC3339 (UTC) or "" when the connection has never
passed a check (BAR-5678). Populated by the LIST path only — the
single-row mutations answer "", the same law as the org responses.

linked_credential_id.description: LinkedCredentialID is set on link-mode rows of every provider.

region.description: Region is the S3-family region (issue #3874); empty for azblob rows.

days.description:
Days is the override in days. 1–90 any member; 91–365 admin rank
only; null clears the override.

Days is the days-mode lifetime; ignored while DeleteWhenRunEnds
stands (SetRetention's law — the caller may send either shape).

Days is the days-mode lifetime in days; null under
delete-when-run-ends.

deleteWhenRunEnds.description: DeleteWhenRunEnds is the delete-when-run-ends mode's flag.

bucket.description:
Bucket is the ruling-14 default bucket's NAME — null when the org
has no connected bucket (never a fabricated name).

retention.description:
Retention is the org's effective setting in the settings row's
shape (the usage card renders it beside the bytes).

storedBytes.description:
StoredBytes is SUM(size) over the org's state='finalized' rows
only (expired rows' bytes are released; created rows are transient
chunks).

finalizedAt.description: FinalizedAt is the finalize stamp (nil while created).

retentionDays.description:
RetentionDays is the row's EFFECTIVE lifetime in days — the
override when set, else the org policy's days mode; nil when the
org policy is delete-when-run-ends and the row carries no override
(the artifact lives until the run ends per the mode).

machine_poll_expires_at.description:
MachinePollExpiresAt is the credential's expiry (the 24h
machine-poll TTL), rendered when the token is.

machine_poll_token.description:
MachinePollToken is the machine chain's credential PLAINTEXT,
returned exactly once on the assignment that minted it (epic 164
entry 12): the machine presents it as
`Authorization: Bearer <token>` on /api/v1/runner/machine/*. Only
the hash rests server-side. Empty on every other read — the
plaintext is never shown twice.

duplicate.description:
Duplicate is true when this completion is the idempotent replay of
an already-registered attempt — the SAME revision came back and
no second row exists.

at.description: At is the event's server stamp (unix seconds).

detail.description: Detail is the server's one-line record of the action.

kind.description:
Kind is the action's word (promotion | eviction | trim |
cold_fill | refusal).

scope.description: Scope is the event's cache scope.

total.description: Total is the pre-cap ledger size (the events surface's shape).

hits.description:
Hits/Warms are the scope's toolchain hit and warm counts (the
separate-captioned-values law — never one merged number).

posture.description:
Posture is the scope's rw/ro posture (the trust decision the
server made — the page's chip, with the trusted-refs sentence as
its caption).

scope.description:
Scope is the scope's name (org- or repo-scoped, the host's
naming).

size_bytes.description: SizeBytes is the scope's current size on the host volume.

access_key_id_masked.description:
AccessKeyIDMasked is the stored access key id with its middle
replaced (the page renders the identifier, never a secret, never
the raw id).

attached.description:
Attached marks the org's resolved key for its provider — the one
the machine-create custody chain unseals into the spot adapter's
per-exec config.

attached_pools.description:
AttachedPools names the pool specs referencing this key (empty
until the packing-declaration store lands — the attach is
org-level until then).

created_at.description: CreatedAt is the key's store stamp (unix seconds).

key_id.description: KeyID is the stored key's id.

name.description: Name is the org's display label for the key.

provider.description:
Provider is the cloud the key serves (aws today — the spot arm's
provider vocabulary; gcp/azure are the design's accepted set but
have no verifier, so they refuse at the verify-and-store).

region.description:
Region is the cloud region the key serves (the adapter's config
needs it for every machine identity).

access_key_id.description: AccessKeyID is the key's public identifier half.

name.description: Name is the org's display label for the key.

provider.description:
Provider is the cloud the key serves (aws today — the only
provider with a live verifier).

region.description: Region is the cloud region the key serves (required for aws).

secret_access_key.description:
SecretAccessKey is the key's secret half. TLS-only: the live
check consumes it, the seal stores it encrypted, nothing logs it.

orphaned.description:
Orphaned: the connection's state is suspended/removed — the
mapping is reported, and placement must never consume it.

profileArchived.description:
ProfileArchived: the mapped profile row is archived — reported,
never silently dropped (the release-archive case stays visible).

profileName.description: ProfileName is the mapped profile's runs-on name.

connectedAt.description: ConnectedAt is the installation row's creation, RFC3339.

githubOrg.description: GithubOrg is the installation's GitHub account login.

id.description:
ID is the installation ROW id (the connection id the client hands
back on the detail/save paths), string on the wire.

installationId.description: InstallationID is GitHub's id for the installation.

repoCount.description:
RepoCount is the installation's mapping rows (its repositories
with a saved profile answer).

state.description: State is the derived connection state (the vocabulary above).

preinstalled.description:
Preinstalled is the comma-joined column split onto the wire array
(the profile labels' transport shape) — last: the pinned
fieldalignment analyzer wants the pointer word trailing here
(review round 1 verified with the standalone analyzer).

releaseState.description:
ReleaseState is the closed available|archived vocabulary, derived
from the row's Archived bool (the D1 decision: one fact, one
column, the state rendered on the wire).

openWindow.description:
OpenWindow is the open window's live percentile answer; nil when
nothing qualifies (an idle org).

reason.description:
Reason carries "no data" when the requested profile (or the org)
holds no insights rows at all; empty otherwise.

series.description:
Series is the concurrency series, raw for the most recent 24
hours and hourly for every older rolled hour (newest first).

windows.description:
Windows are the pinned windows (newest first, capped at the most
recent 168 WINDOWS — whole windows, never split across metrics),
or only ?window='s hour when given.

durationP50Ms.description:
The four percentile values, milliseconds. Nil = no qualifying
rows for that metric.

pinnedAt.description:
PinnedAt is the pin stamp on a pinned window; nil on the live
open window.

profile.description: Profile is the stat's profile ('' = unprofiled / org-wide).

windowStart.description: WindowStart is the window the stat describes (UTC hour).

conclusion.description:
Conclusion is GitHub's workflow_job.conclusion (github rows
only; empty until a completed delivery lands).

jobRef.description:
JobRef is the execution's reference; (source, jobRef) resolves
the detail.

logBlobDigest.description:
LogBlobDigest is the sha256 of the captured gzip log in the org's
bucket — the log read's handle. Empty = never captured.

queueWaitSeconds.description:
QueueWaitSeconds / DurationSeconds are the view's NULL-armed
computations; null = unknown, never zero (D2).

repo.description:
Repo / Workflow / Profile / Runner / State / Result /
GithubLogURL ride the ledger row verbatim (the list's contract).

sourceId.description:
SourceID + Source are the row's identity ((source, sourceId));
Source is "pool" | "builder" | "github".

startedAt.description:
StartedAt / CompletedAt / LogUploadedAt: the first two are
GITHUB'S own stamps (the mirror's source of truth; null when
GitHub never sent one), the third the capture's commit moment
(null until the first capture).

durationSeconds.description:
DurationSeconds is the server-computed run duration; null when
live or the source records no terminal timestamp.

githubLogUrl.description:
GithubLogURL is the GitHub job's log page (P1.11's link-out);
empty for the other sources.

hosted.description:
Hosted is true only for github rows: a GitHub-hosted job BMC
never ran.

jobRef.description:
JobRef is the execution's reference: the pool job id, the
builder's RunReference#attempt, GitHub's job id.

profile.description:
Profile stays empty in v1 (the placement note lives on the
refusals, B2.5).

queueWaitSeconds.description:
QueueWaitSeconds is the server-computed queue wait; null =
unknown, never zero (D2).

repo.description:
Repo is the repository (the github source's repository name;
empty for the BMC-run sources in v1).

result.description: Result is the terminal reason / conclusion; empty while live.

runId.description: RunID is GitHub's workflow run id (0 for the BMC-run sources).

runner.description:
Runner is the machine the execution ran on (the pool VM's
provider id, the builder's machine agent id; empty for github
rows — GitHub-hosted, BMC never ran them).

sourceId.description:
SourceID is the source row's id as text; (source, sourceId) is
the row's identity.

state.description: State is the source's state verbatim.

cleanupDiskPercent.description:
CleanupDiskPercent: 0 = not configured; 10-90 = auto cleanup when
the disk crosses this percent full.

delivery.description:
Delivery states when the setting reaches the machine (the dual-path
contract, on the wire so the panel can say it honestly).

bound.description:
Bound: true = a live runner binding (runner_pool_enlistments row,
released_at IS NULL); false = unbound, available to Add.

cleanupDiskPercent.description:
CleanupDiskPercent is the machine's auto disk-cleanup threshold
(AAR.5 item 3): 0 = not configured, else the stored 10-90 band
value. The setting's own read/write rides the cleanup route.

credentialState.description:
CredentialState is B1.7's visible rotation state; empty (omitted)
on healthy machines — B1.1 always omits it.

currentJobId.description: CurrentJobID is the running job's id while the lifecycle is busy.

drain.description:
Drain is the machine's live transition bookkeeping (B1.4): present
while the machine is draining, quarantined-with-a-pending-drain or
returning. The overdue flag is the drain-timeout REPORT — the
operator's signal that the force option is open.

labelProbe.description:
LabelProbe is the label-probe verdict: "pass" only when verified
runner capability evidence is on record (AAR.2's evidence law —
never a default pass), else "unknown".

labelProbeVerifiedAt.description:
LabelProbeVerifiedAt is the AGE of that evidence: the oldest
verified_at across the required labels on a pass, the retained
last-good timestamp on a downgraded probe, omitted when no probe
ever ran (B1.5).

lastJobId.description:
LastJobID is the machine's most recent job (live first, then the
latest terminal); empty when it never ran one.

needsAttention.description:
NeedsAttention is the quarantine surface's state flag (AAR.5 item
4): true while the machine holds quarantined — the panel renders
"needs attention / re-enlist" from it. Re-enlist is the return
action (the existing lifecycle service); there is no silent untag
path (release refuses from quarantined — the transition table).

owner.description: Owner is the owning org's name.

profilesServed.description:
ProfilesServed names the profiles this machine can serve; empty in
B1.1 (B2.2's profile read lands the vocabulary).

providerId.description:
ProviderID is the pool's join key (GH #4141): the machine's
virtual_machines row id as a string — the id space the job ledger's
runner column (runner_jobs.vm_provider_id, minted by the floor as
the VM row id) and the connections detail's runnerIds carry. The
frontend joins machines to ledger rows and connection runners
through it (in live mode the agent-row id matches neither).
Empty (omitted) on an agent row with no VM behind it.

scope.description:
Scope / Ownership surface the machine's live binding's pool scope
and ownership class (AAR.5 item 1, GH #3206): "org"/"customer_owned"
on every self-hosted machine in this org's list — the org surface
only ever creates org-scope, customer-owned bindings. Empty on an
unbound row (there is no binding to classify).

todayRuns.description:
TodayRuns / TodayMinutes are today's (UTC) completed runs and
metered minutes for THIS machine — the phase-1 pages' per-row
facts (P1.3's list, P1.6's detail).

deadline.description:
Deadline is the drain's report bound — Overdue goes true at it and
the force option opens.

jobId.description: JobID is the job a pending drain waits on.

overdue.description:
Overdue is the drain-timeout REPORT (AC4): true once the deadline
passed with the drain still pending.

pendingAction.description:
PendingAction is what the standing drain resolves into ("release"
or "quarantine"); "" on a held or returning machine.

requestedAt.description: RequestedAt is when the standing transition was issued.

confirm_kind_removal.description:
ConfirmKindRemoval is the coexistence consent law's explicit
confirmation — required when the PUT removes a kind the org's
live machines still serve.

consent_record.description:
ConsentRecord is control 5 (consent point → decision); omitted
points keep their defaults.

org_default_runner_version.description:
OrgDefaultRunnerVersion is the org-default pin the
pinned_org_default posture requires.

bound.description:
Bound: true = a live runner binding (runner_pool_enlistments row,
released_at IS NULL); false = unbound, available to Add.

cleanupDiskPercent.description:
CleanupDiskPercent is the machine's auto disk-cleanup threshold
(AAR.5 item 3): 0 = not configured, else the stored 10-90 band
value. The setting's own read/write rides the cleanup route.

credentialState.description:
CredentialState is B1.7's visible rotation state; empty (omitted)
on healthy machines — B1.1 always omits it.

currentJobId.description: CurrentJobID is the running job's id while the lifecycle is busy.

drain.description:
Drain is the machine's live transition bookkeeping (B1.4): present
while the machine is draining, quarantined-with-a-pending-drain or
returning. The overdue flag is the drain-timeout REPORT — the
operator's signal that the force option is open.

needsAttention.description:
NeedsAttention is the quarantine surface's state flag (AAR.5 item
4): true while the machine holds quarantined — the panel renders
"needs attention / re-enlist" from it. Re-enlist is the return
action (the existing lifecycle service); there is no silent untag
path (release refuses from quarantined — the transition table).

profilesServed.description:
ProfilesServed names the profiles this machine can serve; empty in
B1.1 (B2.2's profile read lands the vocabulary).

providerId.description:
ProviderID is the pool's join key (GH #4141): the machine's
virtual_machines row id as a string — the id space the job ledger's
runner column (runner_jobs.vm_provider_id, minted by the floor as
the VM row id) and the connections detail's runnerIds carry. The
frontend joins machines to ledger rows and connection runners
through it (in live mode the agent-row id matches neither).
Empty (omitted) on an agent row with no VM behind it.

scope.description:
Scope / Ownership surface the machine's live binding's pool scope
and ownership class (AAR.5 item 1, GH #3206): "org"/"customer_owned"
on every self-hosted machine in this org's list — the org surface
only ever creates org-scope, customer-owned bindings. Empty on an
unbound row (there is no binding to classify).

todayRuns.description:
TodayRuns / TodayMinutes are today's (UTC) completed runs and
metered minutes for THIS machine — the phase-1 pages' per-row
facts (P1.3's list, P1.6's detail).

busy.description: Busy is the flavor's slices serving a job (the boundJobId set).

total.description: Total is the flavor's live slices on the host.

warm.description:
Warm is the flavor's slices held as warm stock (idle past their
job or created ahead of demand).

flavors.description:
Flavors carries the per-flavor counts (newest flavor first by
name — the grouping is deterministic, the page adds no sort).

pool_id.description:
PoolID is the packing host's id (the compound slice provider id's
parent path — the census's grouping key).
