slice_count.description: SliceCount is the host's live slices across flavors.

bound_job_id.description:
BoundJobID is the serving job's reference (empty = the slice is
idle stock).

destroy_pending_at.description:
DestroyPendingAt/Channel are the spot arm's server-recorded
reclaim marks (issue #4254): WHEN the interruption notice landed
and WHICH channel delivered it ('eventbridge' — the control-plane
SQS watcher — or 'metadata_poll', the guest-reported fallback).
The page's reclaim caption names THIS record, never a guest claim.

provider_id.description: ProviderID is the slice's compound id ("<host>/<slice-id>").

status.description: Status is the mirror's lifecycle word (the pool's state machine).

warm.description: Warm marks warm-floor stock (the idle state IS its job).

minimum_job_age_seconds.description:
MinimumJobAgeSeconds is the intake's claim backoff (0 disables it;
default 30).

row_exists.description:
RowExists is whether the org carries a settings row (the warm
opt-in's record). False = the defaults are the answer.

warm_floors.description:
WarmFloors is the per-flavor floor list (empty = the pool
maintains nothing for this org).

warm_pool_gate.description:
WarmPoolGate is the SERVER-recorded warm-gate decision for the org
(feature_gates bmc_runner_warm_pool, fail-closed off). The row's
existence AND the gate must both read on before the pool
maintains anything — the UI's gate-off empty state names this.

imageArchived.description:
ImageArchived is the B3.9 catalogue's fact for the profile's
BaseImageID, resolved live at read time (services/runnerimages'
ArchivedByImageID, one batched query): a release archiving an image
flips every referencing profile's flag without touching profile
rows. Empty BaseImageID → false; an unknown id → false (honest: the
id was never in the catalogue — the seed validation makes this
unreachable for seeded profiles). Additive field (B3.9): the
frontend client type gains it when P1.16 lands.

jobCount.description:
JobCount is 0 in v1, ALWAYS: no join exists today (RunnerJob carries
no profile field), and inventing one would misreport. The field ships
now so the response shape is stable; the count turns live in B2.5's
placement, which stamps the profile on the job record.

minCpuCores.description:
MinCPUCores/MinRAMMb are the shape floors (0 = no floor);
ConcurrencyCap is the per-machine cap (0 = the no-cap default).

daysElapsed.description: UTC calendar days including today (the DECIDED calendar-so-far law)

projection.description: whole minutes: minutesSoFar / daysElapsed × daysInPeriod, rounded

day.description: YYYY-MM-DD, the UTC day of OccurredAt

minutesToday.description: today's UTC minutes, the daily rows' own population

runningJobs.description: runner_jobs in dispatched/running for the org

storageGB.description: the recorded v1 boundary: 0 until the B5.2+ metadata

basis.description: Basis states the counting rules (D1 — the rules ride the answer).

currentPeriod.description:
CurrentPeriod is the open month's projection block; nil when the
requested period is a closed month (a projection of the past
would invent a future).

daily.description:
Daily is the requested period's UTC day × platform rows, day then
platform ascending. The CSV export serves these rows verbatim.

period.description: Period echoes the answer's YYYY-MM period (the default filled in).

platform.description:
Platform is the period's per-platform totals (the daily rows
summed — exactly, no second query).

previousPeriod.description: PreviousPeriod is the calendar month before the requested period.

storage.description:
Storage is the recorded v1 boundary: an empty series with the
reason (artifact metadata arrives with the artifact store stories).

total.description:
Total is the period's total minutes — the daily rows' exact sum of
raw floats (never rounded; the screen may format).

client_envelope.description:
ClientEnvelope is the browser-sealed copy of PrivateSSHKey the server
stores (issue #4424, B8); the plaintext is for the install push only.

parent_connection_id.description:
Bastion/parent connection (nullable)
If set, this connection requires jumping through the parent bastion host

private_key_encrypted_data_id.description:
Encrypted SSH Key (Story 18-14: Refactored to use polymorphic encrypted_data table)
SECURITY FIX: Previously stored plaintext - now encrypted!
References the EncryptedData table where the SSH private key is stored encrypted

use_agent_forwarding.description:
SSH Agent forwarding (when using bastion)
If true, uses bastion's SSH agent instead of a separate key

checked_at.description:
CheckedAt / LastVerifiedAt are RFC3339; LastVerifiedAt is null until a
check succeeds (a failed check must not render as a verification).

active_storage_alerts.description:
ActiveStorageAlerts counts the org's unresolved storage_volume and
storage_bucket alert events — the same active predicate both
per-resource status reads use.

bucket_bytes.description:
BucketBytes sums every bucket's latest snapshot across the org's S3
connections. Null until a bucket snapshot carries bytes (LB-1 not
landed), and never counting a partial snapshot (a lower bound).

volume_used_bytes.description:
VolumeUsedBytes and VolumeProvisionedBytes sum the org's latest volume
readings over one reading set: the volumes that reported BOTH figures.
Null when no volume did. VolumesMeasured counts exactly that set, so
the count and the two sums always name the same volumes.

volumes_full_within_14d.description:
VolumesFullWithin14d counts volumes whose fill projection lands within
14 days. A volume with no real projection (not enough history, no
growth, no capacity) is never counted.

issued_via.description:
IssuedVia records the minting surface (audit provenance:
"destructive-click", "re-approval", "setup-render", "runner-install").

reapproval_id.description:
ReapprovalID closes the stranded ask this mint answers (empty for a
destructive click that is not answering anything).

resolved.description: the ask closed by this intake ("" when none)

account.description:
azblob fields (issue #3576). AccessKey is the storage key; Account the
storage account.

default_bucket.description:
DefaultBucket lets the verify step check a named bucket. For gcs this is
the native probe's Bucket.Attrs target (issue #3879): a credential
scoped to one bucket verifies without project-wide list permission.

linked_credential_id.description:
LinkedCredentialID (issue #3874) verifies a link BEFORE create: the
handler resolves the org-scoped credential through the vault (the vault
gate lives in the handler) and probes with its secret. The
wizard's verify step calls this before create, so a bad link fails
there, not at create.

service_account_json.description:
ServiceAccountJSON is the gcs native credential (issue #3879). When set,
the verify runs over the Cloud Storage API; when empty, a gcs request
keeps the SigV4 path with the HMAC pair (legacy rows).

encryption_key.description:
EncryptionKey is accepted for caller compatibility and ignored: the
trust proof is the device.trust rental's vault-key payload.

target_version.description: TargetVersion is optional — empty upgrades to the catalog's latest.

enabled.description:
Enabled is true when dev mode is being turned ON, false when turned OFF.
The FE only fires this endpoint on the ON transition (the story
specifies "one-time audit signal"); we accept the field anyway so a
future caller can record the OFF transition without an API change.

reused.description:
Reused is true when the mint hit the redelivery-reuse rule (a live,
unconsumed rental already existed for this operation + target).

delivery_public_key.description: DeliveryPublicKey is the raw X25519 public key, base64 on the wire.

confirm.description:
Confirm is the user's fresh consent (the dialog's confirm). Empty on
the first POST — the dialog answer.

destination.description:
Destination + Key are the point's archive handle (the durability
endpoint's point list carries both).

new_install.description:
The clone mode's fields (BAR-4912): NewInstall is the name of the
install to create (required on clone), Data is the explicit
with/without choice (required on clone), and BackupPoint is the
with-data clone's point handle (absent on without).

parallel_install.description:
ParallelInstall is the sibling install a parallel restore lands on.
Required on parallel; the record must already exist.

confirm.description:
Confirm is the purge dialog's fresh consent. A keep-data removal
needs none; the purge refuses its absence (a bare DELETE can never
mint the token).

retain_backup.description:
RetainBackup is Retain Backup: false additionally purges the final
archive and destinations after verification. nil means ON.

retain_data.description:
RetainData is Retain Data (ruling 2026-10-12): false rides the
purge chain, which needs the fresh confirm token. The pointer is
the defaulting law: nil means the ruling's ON.

confirm.description:
Confirm is the user's fresh consent for a migrating upgrade (the
dialog's confirm). Empty on the first POST — the dialog answer.

gates.description:
Story 137.2 (issue #2962) — the rule-10 gate set. Gates is the
upgrade's gate list (v1 evaluates the gateway provider; the reserved
phase-2 provider names refuse at the plan compile below with the
pointed error). Manual-kind gates compile into the plan's
confirmations — the dispatch then demands a fresh confirm token like
a migrating upgrade. Soak is the post-promotion soak window in
seconds (0 = none); RetainOldRevision pins the pre-upgrade revision
across the soak (must cover it — the plan refuses otherwise);
AnalyzeWindow is the pre-switch evaluation window (0 = the 10m
default). Durations ride seconds on the wire, nanoseconds on the
queue payload.

target_digest.description:
TargetDigest is the blueprint target's compile pin (story 165.5,
additive and omitempty): required beside a 40-hex TargetVersion,
refused otherwise — a digestless SHA is never dispatchable.

target_version.description:
TargetVersion is the catalog version the install upgrades to. The
capability filter has already hidden what this engine cannot run.
For a BLUEPRINT stack's update (story 165.5) it is the re-resolved
commit SHA (the 40-hex shape — IsRef's discriminator) and
TargetDigest carries the new compile's pin.

definitions.description:
Definitions is the definition record's status block (entry 9's
shape, entry 6's surfacing): the latest revision's pin and the
source lifecycle's named state, on the surface the user stares at.

preview_note.description:
PreviewNote annotates a DEFERRED delta preview (the mid-roll honesty
gate, mirrored from the route's own gate): a stack transition is in
flight, so the as-deployed capture is about to move and a delta
previewed now would not be the delta the sweeper runs. The preview
resumes once the transition lands (the route refuses dispatching
until then); the compiled-artifact diff still rides.

source_reconnect.description:
SourceReconnect names the D4 reconnect-review path when the source
sits orphaned: a fresh review's confirmed apply mints a new
definition revision and journals the break.

stack_review.description:
StackReview is the SHARED stack transition review's delta (epic
stack-evolution entry 6): a stack parent's lawful set change renders
the entry-2 review — who joins, what they wire to, what dies, the
data fate, the wave plan — instead of the dead-end refusal. Absent
for single-component installs and refused transitions.

linked_release.description:
LinkedRelease is the release of a linked image registry's cloud
credential, required for a registry in cloud_credential mode and refused
otherwise (BAR-1675, ADR-104 D2).

release.description:
Release is the sharer's one-time release of the secret's own value. It is
required when the secret has one, and refused otherwise (ADR-104 D2).

orphaned_since.description:
OrphanedSince carries the orphaned state's since stamp (zero when
connected).

source_state.description: SourceState is "connected" or the named "orphaned" state (D4).

cause.description:
Cause is the named reason verbatim — the workflow note or the
terminal event's message; for a terminal failure with no event
surviving, the record state's cause class.

code.description:
Code is the typed refusal code (issue #4493, additive and omitempty):
the board decides from this field, never from Cause's prose. Set only
on a terminal failure whose newest coded event survives in the window.

kind.description:
Kind is the detail class: "failed" for a terminal failure, "working"
for a live named note (a backoff among them).

refusal.description:
Refusal is the typed deep-link object the Code names (today: the
stranded-records refusal). Absent unless Code names it and its detail
decodes.

build_binding.description:
BuildBinding is the project's git build (BAR-601, additive): the
trigger, repo and branch the stack deploys from, or null. Always
served, like the list entry.

bundle.description:
Bundle is the deployed revision's bundle ref (story 142.5, additive
and omitempty): the installed identity the upgrade affordance needs —
the capability-filtered versions listing is queried with its name and
the running version is named beside the affordance and cut from the
targets. Absent on a record with no deployed revision.

definitions.description:
Definitions is the stack's platform-held definition record (epic
stack-evolution entry 9, additive and omitempty): the latest
revision's pin and the source lifecycle's NAMED state —
"orphaned" when the import repository no longer answers (D4). The
stack keeps running and evolving from stored revisions while
orphaned; the named state is what the panel renders. Absent for
installs with no definition revisions (single-component installs
and every pre-entry-9 stack).

gate_pause.description:
GatePause is the rule-10 gate pause block (story 137.2, issue
#2962, additive and omitempty): when the newest gate progress event
is an OPEN pause, the panel renders the Resume/Abort affordance off
it. Absent on every install whose events carry no open pause.

gitops.description:
Gitops is the install's CI-deploy state section (story 143.2,
additive and omitempty): enabled/reconnect/pending/installed/
abandoned/disabled with the connection, repo coordinates, and the
last CI deploy. Absent when the install carries no gitops surface.

labels.description:
Labels is the record's movable label pointers (story 149.6, additive
and omitempty): name → revision ("next", "staging" — the deploykit
label law), served verbatim so the deploy timeline's revision cards
can join the labels by revision number. A record with no labels
serves no key at all (the pre-149.6 shape).

revisions.description:
Revisions is the per-revision provenance surface (story 143.3,
additive and omitempty): every revision's bundle identity and
provenance, with the CI build subject beside the revisions that
carry one. A nil Build is the MANUAL subject — never inherited (Law
12b): a panel deploy after a CI deploy renders the manual subject on
its own revision while the CI revision keeps its own. The panel's
rollback affordance reads the CI-stamped numbers off this list.

slots.description:
Slots is the stack view's slot panel (epic managed-xyz story 5b,
issue #4085, additive and omitempty): the stack's managed slots with
the SERVER-AUTHORED action list — the rotate action renders from
here, never invented client-side. Absent on a stack that declares
no slots.

build_binding.description:
BuildBinding is the project's git build (BAR-601): the trigger, repo
and branch the stack deploys from, or null when the project has no
single binding. Always served (no omitempty) so the console reads an
explicit null rather than an absent key.

managed_by_stack.description:
ManagedByStack is the managed-slot marker (epic managed-xyz story
4, AC2 — additive and omitempty): the OWNING STACK's install name
when the install is a managed slot's provisioning (a
ManagedSlotBinding claims it). The typed-apps law is "unified list,
per-type surfaces" — slot installs are SHOWN, as managed rows the
FE badges from this field; the install-scoped verbs are fenced by
AC5's refusal (owned by stack; use the stack surface).

namespace.description:
Namespace is the record's PhysicalName (story 149.4, additive and
omitempty): the literal k8s namespace the engine renders everything
into — the stacks surface's pods bridge scopes the K8s View to it.
It equals InstallName at fresh install and diverges permanently
after a restore cutover (the alias law), so the client never
derives it from the install name.

park.description:
Park is the honest-state badge (issue #2709 §2.7, additive and
omitempty): the install's active parked upgrade — a parked app
reads as parked on the list surface too, never only on its detail.

arrival_kind.description:
Arrival is the generic arrival pick ("public" | "tunnel") with its
optional addon instance sub-choice; ZoneID is the registry pick.

blueprint.description:
Blueprint is the deploy wizard's ORIGINALLY SELECTED source (epic
165 story 165.5 — additive and omitempty): the repo + ref + file
the card resolved, persisted at install time so the update flow
re-derives from the SAME selection (the never-silently-switch-
files law). Absent on every pre-165.5 request.

policy_gen.description:
PolicyGen is the store-assigned CAS generation: the write route's
optional policy_gen answer echoes it back, and a stale answer is
the named 409 (BAR-5597 review — the panel's edit door races
exactly like any other write door).

can_request.description:
CanRequest is FALSE at launch: the in-product request door is part
of the strip (backend#4735 item 1), so the payload never advertises
a door it does not open. The field stays in the shape — the v1
console contract reads it, and false keeps the request affordance
hidden with no FE change; the field's removal rides the FE strip
card.

grant.description:
Grant is the ledger row that decided the state (any status) — the
expiry clock the boundary renders from.

pending_request.description:
PendingRequest is set when a pre-launch request is still queued —
"how to get it" cites it (the approver tier still decides it).

expiration_mode.description:
ExpirationMode controls how ExpiresAt behaves (Epic 103 / ADR-078).
  - "fixed"   : hard deadline at ExpiresAt (default; pre-granted windows).
  - "sliding" : ExpiresAt resets on each successful CheckAccess, bounded
                by AbsoluteMaxExpiresAt, advancing by IdleTimeout.

granted_by_id.description: GrantedByID is the admin who created this authorization

idle_timeout.description:
IdleTimeout is the sliding idle window. Nullable; meaningful only when
ExpirationMode == "sliding". On each successful access the grant's
ExpiresAt advances to now+IdleTimeout (capped at AbsoluteMaxExpiresAt).

is_jit.description:
IsJIT marks grants minted by the JIT MFA-elevation flow (Epic 103
wrapper). It is AUDIT METADATA ONLY — CheckAccess treats JIT-originated
and pre-granted rows identically. (The dormant session-blob IsJIT flag
from Story 69.1 was removed in Story 103-5; the flag now lives here.)

last_used_at.description:
LastUsedAt records the most recent successful CheckAccess on a sliding
grant. Updated atomically inside the same transaction that extends
ExpiresAt. Nullable; only set for sliding grants.

member_id.description: MemberID is the ProjectMember receiving access

org_id.description:
OrgID is the target org for org-scope grants (ADR-075 M1). Nullable:
NULL for SA-scope rows. CheckOrgVaultAccess filters on it.

reason.description: Reason is an optional explanation for the access grant

scope.description:
Scope discriminates the grant target (ADR-075 M1 / migration 000043):
  - "sa"  : ServiceAccountID set, OrgID NULL (legacy shape, default)
  - "org" : OrgID set, ServiceAccountID NULL (org-vault KEK use)
Enforced at the DB tier by authorized_accesses_scope_target_chk.

service_account_id.description:
ServiceAccountID is the target service account. Nullable: NULL for
org-scope rows (migration 000043 dropped the NOT NULL).

worker_key.description: hex-encoded target worker identity (audit label for the sealed blob's consumer)

encrypted_data_id.description:
EncryptedDataID is the value row the envelope was read from. The browser
sends it back as the release marker when it shares the secret (BAR-1675,
ADR-104 D3). It identifies a row; it carries no key or plaintext.

approve_collisions.description: ApproveCollisions is the staged-import review's grant.

confirms.description:
Confirms echoes the dispatch tokens the dialog minted, per archived
component.

export_key.description: ExportKey pins the export (empty = the stack's latest pickable set).

facts.description:
Facts are the TARGET cluster's context facts (the same source the
install route's resolved payload carries — the panel's cluster
context). The import compiles against them; a dispatch without them
refuses at the worker.

source_cluster_id.description:
SourceClusterID names the cluster the export ran on (the set's
recorded scope; same project — the copy is same-org, the move threat
model is not this story's door to open).

stack.description: Stack is the stack manifest's name the export recorded.

fence.description:

Confirms echoes the dispatch tokens the dialog minted — the

export_key.description: ExportKey pins the export (empty = the stack's latest pickable set).

compiles against them).

flavor.description:
Flavor is the move path: "cold" (the fence-first default) or
"replication" (the fast path — refused unless the recorded set's
every stateful-authoritative member declared `move: replication`;
an incapable set is NEVER silently downgraded, it is refused with
the cold path named). Empty means cold.

retire.description:
Retire is the source-retirement choice — explicit, never a default:
"keep-data" (the retired-original tombstone as standing
cancellation) or "purge" (destroy; the move's target probe gate is
the verification).

source_cluster_id.description:
SourceClusterID names the cluster the export ran on (the set's
recorded scope; same project — the SAME-ORG gate runs against the
source cluster's recorded org).

stack.description: Stack is the stack manifest's name the export recorded.

migrate_existing_backups.description: MigrateExistingBackups turns a destination switch into a migration.

migration_cleanup.description:
MigrationCleanup is the old-destination deletion consent ("keep" |
"delete_after_cutover"); never honored without the migrate choice.

error.example: Rate limit exceeded. Maximum: 10 jobs/minute. Try again in 45 seconds.

auto_window_hours.description:
AutoWindowHours: the rollout window the auto path's candidate rule
reads (design §3.5: connected-or-window agents). Default 24.

id.description: ID is the surrogate key (BIGSERIAL in migration 000170).

mode.description:
Mode: manual (default) | auto. The story-5 worker enrolls only auto
orgs; manual orgs update by explicit click only.

org_id.description: OrgID: the owning organization; UNIQUE — the one-row-per-org law.

pinned_version.description:
PinnedVersion: the org's version pin (NULL = unpinned). Rail-verified
at write time; auto rollouts skip pinned orgs, manual clicks target
the pin.

acknowledged_at.description:
AcknowledgedAt/By and ResolvedAt/By record who acted and when (BAR-496).
Acknowledge also sets the Acknowledged bool above, which stays the
read the firing list filters on.

dedup_key.description:
DedupKey names one alert occurrence. A second insert with the same
(org, key) is a no-op, so an alert raised by a repeating sweep is
stored and delivered once. Missed-backup alerts use
"backup-missed:<cluster>:<lane>:<target>:<window start>" (BAR-496).
NULL for every other alert, so the partial index ignores them.

severity.description: Severity copies the firing rule's severity (AlertSeverity*).

target_kind.description:
TargetKind/TargetID/TargetName mirror the firing rule's target
(AlertTarget*). Pre-158.3 rows read as vm_threshold with target_id 0
— their vm_id is the subject, unchanged.

condition.description:
Condition is the watched condition (IsValidAlertCondition's per-kind
vocabulary). Empty for vm_threshold rules.

scope.description:
Scope says which resources a storage_volume rule covers (AlertScope*).
Defaults to resource; other kinds ignore it.

severity.description:
Severity is warning or critical (AlertSeverity*). It rides every fired
event and the notification text. Defaults to warning.

status.description:
Status is the evaluator-owned rule lifecycle surfaced in CRUD
(AlertRuleStatus*). CRUD writes only Active; the sweep owns the
target_missing flip (and never flips it back except through rule
update, which re-arms the rule).

target_id.description:
TargetID is the target resource id for the non-VM kinds (today: the
cluster id for cluster_health and stack_component). Zero for
vm_threshold and platform_signal rules.

target_kind.description:
TargetKind names what the rule watches (AlertTarget*). Defaults to
vm_threshold so pre-158.3 rows (and payloads that omit it) keep their
exact existing meaning.

target_name.description:
TargetName names the sub-target: the stack component name, or the
platform_sensors sensor key. Empty for vm_threshold and cluster_health.

account_id.description:
AccountID is the provider account the token was validated against
at install (R13 — the same-account preflight's arrival half). A
rotation whose token answers from a DIFFERENT account refuses by
name (reinstall the addon to change accounts).

instance.description:
Instance is the addon instance id the route bindings and arrival
facts name (the R1/R13 disambiguator).

last_ensured_at.description:
LastEnsuredAt is when the arrival-ensure last converged this
custody's connectors (the re-ensure pass's success stamp). Nil until
the first pass lands. A row whose TokenRotatedAt is newer than its
LastEnsuredAt is the honest rotation gap the surfaces render.

org_id.description:
OrgID is the tenancy boundary. Several tunnel addon instances may
coexist (R1/R13), so the uniqueness is per (org, provider,
instance).

provider.description: Provider names the tunnel provider ("cloudflare" in v1).

token_rotated_at.description:
TokenRotatedAt is when the custody's token last ROTATED
(RotateSealed — Epic 163 entry 6, FR-7's convergence law). Nil for
install-time captures (Seal): a fresh install's addon flow ensures
its connector right after capture, and there is nothing rotated to
converge. The rotation-convergence pass reads this against
LastEnsuredAt to find the rotated-since-ensure custody rows.

ExpirationMode controls how ExpiresAt behaves (Epic 103 / ADR-078).
  - "fixed"   : hard deadline at ExpiresAt (default; pre-granted windows).
  - "sliding" : ExpiresAt resets on each successful CheckAccess, bounded
                by AbsoluteMaxExpiresAt, advancing by IdleTimeout.

granted_by_id.description: GrantedByID is the admin who created this authorization

idle_timeout.description:
IdleTimeout is the sliding idle window. Nullable; meaningful only when
ExpirationMode == "sliding". On each successful access the grant's
ExpiresAt advances to now+IdleTimeout (capped at AbsoluteMaxExpiresAt).

IsJIT marks grants minted by the JIT MFA-elevation flow (Epic 103
wrapper). It is AUDIT METADATA ONLY — CheckAccess treats JIT-originated
and pre-granted rows identically. (The dormant session-blob IsJIT flag
from Story 69.1 was removed in Story 103-5; the flag now lives here.)

grant. Updated atomically inside the same transaction that extends
ExpiresAt. Nullable; only set for sliding grants.

member_id.description: MemberID is the ProjectMember receiving access

org_id.description:
OrgID is the target org for org-scope grants (ADR-075 M1). Nullable:
NULL for SA-scope rows. CheckOrgVaultAccess filters on it.

reason.description: Reason is an optional explanation for the access grant

scope.description:
Scope discriminates the grant target (ADR-075 M1 / migration 000043):
  - "sa"  : ServiceAccountID set, OrgID NULL (legacy shape, default)
  - "org" : OrgID set, ServiceAccountID NULL (org-vault KEK use)
Enforced at the DB tier by authorized_accesses_scope_target_chk.

service_account_id.description:
ServiceAccountID is the target service account. Nullable: NULL for
org-scope rows (migration 000043 dropped the NOT NULL).

actor_user_id.description:
ActorUserID is the pipeline actor's user (the click's user on a
rollback; the deploy trigger's user on a deploy leg). 0 when the
actor is the pipeline itself.

cluster_id.description:
The deploy identity: the InstallRef triple's cluster + stack plus
the service inside it — the service whose traffic this gate owns
for the run's duration (the one-operation-at-a-time scope).

evidence.description:
Evidence is the probe's output, VERBATIM ([]string as JSON) — the
pass lines on proven, the failure lines on blocked, the leg's
named reason on failed. Never a paraphrase, never an invented
checkmark.

kind.description: Kind is deploy or rollback (the vocabulary above).

org_id.description:
Tenant scope (ADR-062): the run lives inside one org and one
project. Every read binds both halves.

revision_id.description:
The revision this gate ran for — the build_revisions row the leg
deploys (the target on a rollback). RevisionID is the row id the
timeline resolves its health fact through; Revision is the
human-facing monotonic number; AttemptRef is the revision's
attempt reference (provenance); ImageDigest is the pinned digest
the probe's workload runs.

started_at.description:
StartedAt / FinishedAt bound the run; DurationMs is the measured
wall-clock of the whole gate run (the rollback's ≤30 s budget is
recorded here — measured, not assumed).

state.description:
State is the run's truthful state: running → exactly one of
proven / blocked / failed (the vocabulary above).

attempt_ref.description:
AttemptRef is THE idempotency key: "<run_reference>#<attempt>"
(BuildRevisionAttemptRef). UNIQUE — two completions of the same
attempt converge on this one row.

builder_image_digest.description:
BuilderImageDigest is the digest-pinned builder image the build
ran on (the D4 pinning law — provenance survives registry transit).

cluster_id.description:
The deploykit InstallRef triple (D8) plus the service inside the
stack: (cluster_id, stack, service) names the deploy unit the
revision was built for. The (stack, service, revision) half is
UNIQUE inside the tenancy scope — idx_build_revision_identity.

commit.description: Commit is the source commit the build ran against.

credential_ref.description:
CredentialRef is the minted credential's reference (D8's payload):
the attempt's KindBuild token LOOKUP HASH (the #1511 keyed-hash
form, 64 hex chars — a reference, never the plaintext secret, and
hash-at-rest is the storage law). Copied from the attempt ledger
row at acceptance.

image_digest.description:
ImageDigest is the produced image's digest ("sha256:<64 hex>" —
the publish shape discipline the revision registry adopts from
gitops publish.go). RegistryRef is the registry repository
reference the digest was verified in (host/repository). Together
they render the pinned reference: RegistryRef + "@" + ImageDigest.

org_id.description:
Tenant scope (ADR-062): the revision lives inside one org and one
project. Every read binds org+project — a cross-org read is a
miss, never a wildcard. Both halves ride the identity unique index
(mirroring migration 000122's six-column form).

outcome.description:
Outcome is the verified completion's outcome. A revision row
exists only for a verified publish (publish-before-pin, D7), so
today the only value is "succeeded"; the column is the D8
payload's outcome field, carried for the schema's completeness.

plan.description:
Plan is the resolved build block (the Session-32 grammar as
compiled) — the JSON the plan was built from, stored verbatim so
a pruned image can be re-built from the plan + commit (design §12
question 2's answer).

revision.description:
Revision is the monotonic per-identity number (1, 2, 3, ... —
assigned by the repository layer, never a caller's claim).

trigger_source.description:
TriggerSource is what asked for the deploy (the trigger_source
grammar above): written once at registration, never updated —
the append-only law covers it like every other column.

addons.description:
── The platform's Add-ons decision (epic app-platform story 3.4) ──

Addons records the wizard Add-ons step's checkbox set at formation: a
JSON array of keys from the CLOSED set below (monitoring, public_entry,
databases, log_book), in the client's selection order. Empty ('[]' —
the column default) = no addons: every pre-3.4 row, the import path,
and API creates that omit the field. The create gate (handlers/
clusters.go + ClusterServiceImpl.ProvisionClusterBYOV) validates the
keys pre-row; an unknown key never lands.

HONEST SCOPE (story 3.4): of the four keys, only 'monitoring' has a
real install path today — the formation-completion hook (the
WriteK8sClusterImportResult success leg) creates the in-cluster
MonitoringStack (ADR-061) and enqueues the existing Helm provision
task. 'public_entry' (the deploykit gateway addon fires inside the
app-deploy workflow — no standalone formation-time ensure exists),
'databases' (the real lane is the user-driven DatabaseConfiguration
flow — an auto-deploy would invent a name, sizing, and a vault context
the user never chose), and 'log_book' (no log-aggregation surface
exists) persist as DECLARED: the detail surface lists them, nothing
fake-installs them. The addon set is exposed on the platform detail
response (enrichClusterFields) — the add/remove-later management
endpoint is future work.

adopted.description:
Adopted records the D3 ADOPT decision (story 124.3, constraint 4):
creation's contamination preflight found pre-existing, RUNNING,
same-version k3s on EVERY member and the caller explicitly opted in
with adopt_existing. Adopted means BMC installed NO k3s on any member
(SetupNode's k3s step is skipped downstream); the D9 canonical
predicate bmc_installed_k3s = (origin==created && !adopted) keys on
this column, and adopted clusters are panel-only (D8).

agent_image_tag.description:
AgentImageTag is the bmc-agent-k8s image tag last applied to this
cluster's agent Deployment — by cluster import or by the
backend-driven update (agent-update epic story 6, GH #3369 AC3).
Ending the uncommanded drift means the platform can ANSWER "what is
this cluster running" without reading the cluster. Empty = unknown /
pre-story-6 row.

agent_image_tag_previous.description:
AgentImageTagPrevious is the tag that ran before the last apply —
the manual-recovery record (story 6 AC2): no server-side rollback
exists (roll-forward is the law), so the operator reads THIS column
to know what to put back when an applied image proves bad.

backup_plan.description:
── The platform's backup decision (epic app-platform story 3.3) ──

BackupPlan records the wizard Backup step's radio choice at formation:
"daily", "hourly", or "none". Empty string = no decision recorded —
every pre-3.3 row, the import path, and API creates that omit the
field read back as unconfigured (never as a claimed "none": an
explicit no-backups decision and an unconfigured row are different
facts, and the surfaces must not conflate them).

BackupRetentionDays is the PLAN-IMPLIED retention (daily=7, hourly=30,
none=0) — derived server-side at the create gate, never client-set, so
the retention promise on every surface stays the engine's own number.

BackupS3ConnectionID references the org's vault-guarded S3 connection
backups land in (s3_connections.id). Non-nil only when the plan is
daily/hourly — the create gate (handlers/clusters.go +
ClusterServiceImpl.ProvisionClusterBYOV) rejects an on-plan create
whose connection is missing or belongs to another org, pre-row.

HONEST SCOPE (story 3.3, updated by story S2 / #3883): this is the
decision record, validated at the create gate, and the backup executor
now schedules from it (services/backupexec, run by the worker): cluster
state per formation, operator-native Postgres/MariaDB backups, and the
volume lane's wiring. Volumes are not captured yet (the agent-side file
tier is not shipped), and the wizard deliberately OMITS the mockup's
"verified by an automatic restore test" footnote: drills exist as
scripts, but no restore test runs automatically per formation.

backup_s3_connection_id.description:
The index name matches migration 000158's idx_clusters_backup_s3_connection
exactly — the unnamed `index` tag would auto-mint a second, differently
named index over the same column (naming drift between AutoMigrate and
the migration).

engine_epoch.description:
EngineEpoch is the authority epoch: monotonic, bumped by the flip
service under the row lock. Zero for never-flipped clusters.

engine_mode.description:
── The per-cluster engine authority record (Epic 145 story 145.2,
GH #2623; grill Q1) ──

Deploy authority for the customer plane lives HERE as a record:
engine = bmc | in-cluster plus a monotonic epoch, flipped
transactionally at the migration wizard's cutover (story 145.7).
The BMC engine is fenced at ITS dispatch chokepoint on the
customer-plane leg ONLY (story 145.4; catalog-plane dispatch is
mode-independent per R1a); the in-cluster engine checks the
authority at its job-completion boundaries. The write path is
services/engineauthority — the ONLY writer; the epoch strictly
advances (revert plus re-migration advances it; concurrent flips
cannot regress it). No distributed lock: the wizard sequences
drain, flip, assume.

EngineMode defaults to 'bmc' — every pre-145 cluster reads
today's behavior.

engine_namespaces.description:
EngineNamespaces is the DECLARED namespace set the wizard declares at
cutover (grill Q3, ruled option b): the engine's authority answer
carries it, specs validate their namespace-bearing fields against it
at parse time, and the engine's RBAC binds exactly there. JSON array
of strings; typed shape via EngineNamespaceSet.

engine_tier_v_capable.description:
EngineTierVCapable is the Tier V capability flag (the plan: node-host
runners via the agent's job handler) — flipped by the wizard's Tier V
disclosure consent through the engineauthority write path. The
CAPABILITY CHECK against specs is story 145.5's, at schedule time.

headscale_enabled.description:
Headscale mesh networking (Story 51-2).
HeadscaleUserID added in Epic 100 Story 100-2: canonical numeric ID
assigned by Headscale at CreateUser time, persisted so the teardown
path (DisableClusterMesh / DeleteUserByID) doesn't have to derive the
name from the DB row. Mirrors Network.MeshNetworkConfig.HeadscaleUserID.
See ADR-058 for the direct-headscale cluster-mesh path.

ingress_adopted.description:
IngressAdopted records the imported cluster owner's EXPLICIT consent
(story 133.3, GH #2200 AC 2): a live traefik held the cluster's
ingress at import time and the owner accepted the platform's caddy
gateway addon taking it over (traefik stops serving ingress). The
engine honors this recorded decision at every later gateway ensure —
without it, the addon refuses with the named ErrTraefikIngressConsent
(never a silent takeover). Honorable only while the adoption is
lossless (no Traefik-native CRD routes); that check is the engine
rule's, at every use.

SCHEMA NOTE (review L5, story 133.3): this column currently exists
through GORM AutoMigrate alone. The established convention (the
sibling Adopted column, migrations 20260830154357 and 20260829190024) pairs a struct
column with an idempotent `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` goose migration
so both schema paths converge; no such migration has landed here yet.
A future timestamped add_clusters_ingress_adopted migration following the
sibling-migration template is
the owed follow-up if production schema truth is expected to include
this column before AutoMigrate runs.

install_config.description:
InstallConfig carries per-cluster overrides for the k8s distribution installer
(e.g. {"snapshotter":"native"} for nested-container tests). Keys not recognized
by the distribution are passed through as --key=value install flags. Empty/nil
means "use distribution defaults" — no flags are forced. This is persisted so
crash-resume and asynq retries retain the caller's intent.

k8s_version.description: Cluster metadata fields for imported clusters

managed_class.description:
ManagedClass is the platform's STORED class (story C8, #3974, plan
§5a — destructive-consequences-2026-10-27.md): whose account the
platform's machines live on. 'managed' = BMC's cloud account (members
carry VirtualMachine.AccessMode='platform'); 'user' = the user's own
account (AccessMode='byov' — BYOV, user cloud key, multipass).

Written ONCE at creation from the founding members (an import row is
'user' by definition), and enforced against EVERY membership write
afterwards — a cross-class machine is refused with
platform_class_mismatch, never absorbed: a platform's class never
changes by adding machines. Empty means the row predates the column
and the migration has not backfilled it; services.PlatformManagedClass
is the ONE accessor — it derives from the current members, stamps the
derived answer, and every consumer reads the class through it (never
a fresh member scan, never origin heuristics).

operation_generation.description:
OperationGeneration is D6's serialization counter: every mutating
action CASes WHERE operation_generation = N and bumps it. Zero for
never-mutated rows. See services/cluster_operation_cas.go.

replaced_existing.description:
ReplacedExisting records the customer's BAR-3685 replace confirmation
(BAR-3707): at creation the contamination preflight found pre-existing
Kubernetes on at least one member (newer, older, or matching; running
or stopped), the console showed the ONE confirm prompt, and the create
came back with replace_existing. True means formation CLEAN-INSTALLS
our pinned version over whatever was on the machines — SetupNode runs
its uninstall-then-probe leg first; it never silently keeps a foreign
install (that silent keep is exactly what install_k3s's
already_installed path would otherwise report on a matching-version
cluster). The column — not the job payload — is the durable truth the
install worker reads on every (re)dispatch, the same contract as the
sibling Adopted column.

status_since.description:
StatusSince is the wall-clock of the last Status TRANSITION — the FE's
"since <time>" pill suffix truth. Stamped by the shared
RecordClusterStatusTransition helper; rows written before epic-124
carry NULL and the payload omits the field.

sub_status.description:
SubStatus is the machine-written lifecycle refinement of Status
(epic-124 story 124.5). THIS story ships the column + the type-safe
value set only — each value's WRITER lands with its own story
(124.6 installing_* / waiting_agent, 124.9 healing | deadline_exhausted,
124.10 retrying_agent + action_required resolutions). Empty string means
"no sub-state" (the value every pre-124.5 row reads back as).

phase.description:
Phase is the install-lifecycle checkpoint (resume source of truth).
Primary path (issue #1438): pending→setting_up→joining→ready, with
"failed" as a resettable terminal (stuck nodes converge to it via the
per-node timeout).

cluster_id.description:
ClusterID is the NEW claimant cluster the consented deploy targets —
the deploy whose dns-apply payload stamps this consent consumes it.
A consent never matches a deploy from any other cluster.

consented_at.description:
ConsentedAt is the recording instant (the wire consent's recorded_at,
RFC3339 UTC on the wire).

consented_by_user_id.description:
ConsentedByUserID is the org admin/owner who recorded the consent
(the audit attribution; the wire consent's recorded_by rides it).

consumed_at.description:
ConsumedAt is when a consented deploy took the record over (or a
newer consent superseded this one). NULL means the consent is LIVE.

foreign_arrival.description:
ForeignArrival is the live record's tag arrival (the identity's
other half — stamped onto the wire consent verbatim, and the claim
release's narrowing term when non-empty).

foreign_cluster_id.description:
ForeignClusterID is the live record's tag identity VERBATIM (the
numeric cluster row id in string form — the engine's ownership-tag
grammar). The stamped wire consent carries it verbatim, and the
executor's re-assertion compares it to the live tag.

foreign_cluster_row_id.description:
ForeignClusterRowID is the tag identity resolved to the live cluster
row at record time — the OLD claimant whose host claim the terminal
consumption releases (never the whole-cluster release: only this
host's row lets go).

host.description:
Host is the migrated hostname, normalized (lowercase, no trailing
dot — the registry's FQDN form).

id.description: ID is the row's surrogate key (the revoke endpoint's path id).

org_id.description:
OrgID is the hard tenancy boundary: every read and write runs
org-scoped. It leads both indexes (the live-consent read and the
consume's scan are org-scoped first).

record_type.description:
RecordType is the DNS record type the availability check reported
(informational — the engine's executor reads the live record set).

zone_id.description:
ZoneID is the registered zone row the hostname lives in (the
registry's org-scoped table; the consent is zone-scoped because the
record's custody is).

legacy_migrated.description:
LegacyMigrated is the MIGRATION MARKER (R12 round 9): the legacy
lane's resolution key. A stored 133.1-era plan (provider cloudflare,
no ZoneRef) resolves ONLY the org's marker-carrying row — never a
First() over all cloudflare rows. Exactly one row per org+provider
carries the marker (the 133.1 cardinality); deleting the adopted
zone strands the legacy lane into the zone-gone class.

nameservers.description:
Nameservers is the provider's DECLARED nameserver set at connect
(comma-joined, normalized — no trailing dots). The deploy preflight
compares the live TLD-parent delegation against this stored set and
refuses a mismatch (R15 C3: the green-but-dark trap).

org_id.description:
OrgID is the tenancy boundary; the (org, zone_fqdn) pair is the
natural key.

provider_account_id.description:
ProviderAccountID is the provider account the zone lives in
(R13 — load-bearing for the same-account preflight). Captured at
connect from the zone listing response at zero extra cost; ADOPTED
rows carry it empty until the first Cloudflare-tunnel preflight
lazily backfills it (an empty account id NEVER passes the preflight
silently, R13 round 7).

provider_zone_id.description: ProviderZoneID is the provider's opaque zone id.

status.description:
Status is the zone's health posture (the ZoneStatus* vocabulary
above: active | amber | the three drift classes).

verified_at.description:
VerifiedAt is when the zone last passed a live classification
(connect or preflight). Nil for adopted rows until their first
preflight.

zone_fqdn.description:
ZoneFQDN is the zone's fully qualified domain name (no trailing
dot, punycode form).

maintenance: long-TTL, renewable monthly (§8 proposed cadence)
rotation: the pin validity bound (the dual-key window is at most one mandate cycle)

api_base.description:
APIBase is the connection's optional API base — the self-hosted
Forgejo instance ROOT (issue #3644; the provider client appends
/api/v1). A plain URL, never a secret: it rides the row, NOT the
vault. Empty = the provider default (Codeberg for forgejo). Only a
forgejo row may carry a non-empty base; the service refuses one on
the pinned-base providers (github/gitlab) and the plain-git
provider — at write time and again at every use.

auth_kind.description:
AuthKind is the credential SHAPE (story 145.2): 'token' (the 143.1
default — every pre-145.2 row reads back here) or 'ssh_key' (SSH
private-key material for the plain-git engine path). Material lives
ONLY in the vault either way.

status.description:
Status mirrors ImageRegistry's connection lifecycle. LastTestedAt is
the tested-at stamp Law 7's reconnect state reads — never guessed.

verifying_agent_id.description:
VerifyingAgentID is the connection's ONE designated verifying machine
(issue #4328; design zero-trust-sealed-delivery-2026-11-10 SD5, the
v1 designation rule: one verifying machine pinned per git connection,
chosen at bind from the org's trusted connected machines). The
webhook edge relays every raw push to this machine for HMAC
verification — the machine is the only holder of the opened secret
(its sealed-delivery row). Nil = no verifying machine pinned (a
connection bound before the sealed-delivery enrollment, or whose pin
was never set): the edge answers 503 — fail closed — exactly as it
does when the pinned machine is untrusted or unreachable. Moving the
pin is a re-seal (the browser re-seals to the new machine's delivery
key); revoking the pinned machine refuses every delivery (SD4).

auth_mode.description:
AuthMode is the explicit auth contract (Story 79.1). Empty on legacy rows;
ResolveAuthMode() derives from Type (+ FK) until backfilled by writes.

aws_credential_id.description: For ECR: AWS credential reference and region

azure_credential_id.description: For ACR: Azure credential reference and login server (for username/password auth)

url.description: Registry endpoint (auto-filled for known types, editable for private)

username.description:
Username for basic auth (Docker Hub, GHCR, private registries)
Password is stored encrypted using polymorphic encrypted_data table

progress.description:
Fine-grained progress roll-up (0–100) and current step label.
Updated by the step writer in the same tx that writes job_steps.
List queries read these columns directly — no N+1 on job_steps.

resource_type.description:
Generic resource link (ADR-060 V6 — replaces cluster_id/vm_id).
"cluster" | "vm" | "database" | "network" | "multipass" | …

status.description:
Coarse status enum (pending → running → completed|failed|cancelled).
Status transitions are driven by a generic mechanism (ADR-060 Option A),
never hand-set by business-logic error handling.

workflow_id.description:
Temporal domain key (e.g. "provision-cluster-42").
Set when the job triggers a Temporal workflow; nil for Asynq-only jobs.

cluster_id.description: deprecated: use ResourceType+ResourceID (ADR-060 V6); 0 if not cluster-scoped

last_attempt_at.description: Story 18.4.1: When we last tried this step

resource_id.description: ADR-060 V6: the row id of ResourceType

kinds.description:
Kinds is the preset's co-hosting set — at least two DISTINCT
kinds (a single-kind "preset" is just kinds_allowed and would
only blur the law's question).

parent_connection_id.description:
Bastion/parent connection (nullable)
If set, this connection requires jumping through the parent bastion host

private_key_encrypted_data_id.description:
Encrypted SSH Key (Story 18-14: Refactored to use polymorphic encrypted_data table)
SECURITY FIX: Previously stored plaintext - now encrypted!
References the EncryptedData table where the SSH private key is stored encrypted

use_agent_forwarding.description:
SSH Agent forwarding (when using bastion)
If true, uses bastion's SSH agent instead of a separate key

is_local.description: true for local machine, false for remote

ssh_connection_id.description: Reference to ManagedSSHConnection (the jump host entry)

last_seen_at.description: Last seen tracks when the agent last reported this VM's state

draft_name.description:
DraftName is the cluster name the wizard was heading toward when the
network was created (paired with Purpose=cluster-create).

last_reconcile_at.description:
LastReconcileAt is the timestamp of the most recent reconciler touch.
Used for observability + to detect reconciler stalls.

purpose.description:
Purpose is the durable cluster-create draft intent (124.17): "" for
ordinary networks, "cluster-create" for wizard-created drafts. See the
NetworkPurpose docs. GORM AutoMigrate (dev-stage policy) adds the column
on next boot; 000055 keeps the goose path convergent.

reconcile_attempts.description:
ReconcileAttempts is incremented by the Story 101-12 Temporal reconciler
every time it retries a stuck row. When it reaches MaxReconcileAttempts
(10) the row flips to NetworkStatusErrorPermanent. GORM AutoMigrate
(dev-stage policy) adds the column on next boot.

status_reason.description:
StatusReason carries the human-readable failure reason for the visible
failed / delete_failed states (#2359, #2362). Empty on healthy rows.

last_node_left_at.description:
LastNodeLeftAt is stamped by the story 124.14 membership-free write when
the write removed a network's LAST network_nodes row and nothing (no
node, no cluster binding) remains — the candidate marker the network
reconciler's last-node reap pass (ReapLastNodeLeftNetworks) tears the
network down from, after a grace window. Stored INSIDE the Config JSONB
on purpose: the column is already JSONB, so the new key needs NO schema
migration and legacy rows simply read it as nil.

x-enum-comments.NetworkStatusErrorPermanent: Story 101-12: reconciler exhausted retries; needs user action
x-enum-comments.NetworkStatusRemoving: in-flight delete (A-N4); Headscale DeleteUser running async

enabled.description:
Enabled gates delivery: the sink resolves ENABLED channels only.
Disabling is the operator's mute (a disabled channel gets nothing and
hears nothing — no dead-channel notices under the fire-once law).

gorm bool default trap: with `default:true`, Create SKIPS the zero
value, so a struct-literal insert with Enabled:false silently lands
true. Flips go through explicit Updates only — the store creates
channels enabled and never inserts a disabled row (test seeders must
likewise update the column explicitly).

kind.description:
Kind is the channel vocabulary: webhook | email (validated at the
service layer; no DB CHECK constraint — the column is data-safe).

label.description:
Label is the channel's user-chosen, NON-secret display name (epic fcp
entry 6, decision D21): required at create, unique per org — the
service layer validates before every write (a duplicate answers 409
naming the holder) and migration 000152's (org_id, label) unique
index is the at-rest backstop. The label is the rule-form picker's
primary text; the sealed mask stays secondary.

The default:'' is the explorer_grant precedent, NOT a real default:
AutoMigrate runs BEFORE goose at boot, and a plain `not null` ADD
COLUMN against a populated notification_channels table lands
"column contains null values" — boot aborts before 000152 can
backfill. The '' default lets the pre-backfill rows exist for the
seconds between the two; the service layer refuses blank labels on
every write, and 000152 fills the '' cells by created order.

target.description:
Target is the delivery target: for webhook channels the SEALED URL
blob (custody opens it only on the delivery path), for email channels
the address. Never the webhook plaintext.

cadence.description:
Cadence is DigestCadenceWeekly (default) or DigestCadenceDaily (the
opt-in). Validated at the service layer.

include_empty.description:
IncludeEmpty is the empty-summaries opt-in: false (default) means a
quiet window suppresses the digest entirely; true means the org gets
the explicit "all quiet" summary.

org_id.description: OrgID is UNIQUE — one settings row per org.

id.description:
Identity columns: the grant binds the resource's STABLE ID (the
databases uint PK) + org + project + the named person.

reason.description:
Reason is the admin's why (08.3's visibility: the grant carries its
intent alongside its attribution).

shape.description:
The grant vocabulary. Status and Shape are CHECK-constrained at the
DB — migration 000125 adds ck_person_grants_status and
ck_person_grants_shape via idempotent DO-block ALTERs (NOT inline
CREATE TABLE constraints: AutoMigrate runs before goose and creates
this table from these tags, which cannot express a CHECK — the
documented 000040 trap).

arch.description: Arch is the host architecture (the packs' classes must match it).

base.description:
Base is the GENERIC OS base (agent only — nothing runner-shaped
in it, even on our own hosts).

cache.description:
Cache is the pool spec's cache block; a disabled block means no
cache volumes.

cpu_cores.description:
CPUCores and MemoryGB are the host's metal facts (MemoryGB is the
DECLARED unit — the floor's projection converts GB to the MB the
packing arithmetic uses).

enabled.description:
Enabled gates the floor feed: a disabled declaration stays
readable but feeds no floor. NO gorm default tag — a defaulted
bool would omit a false value on struct Create and silently
enable the declaration (the migration's SQL default covers raw
inserts only).

host_id.description: HostID names the real machine — globally unique (see the header).

labels.description: Labels are the capability labels every slice on the host carries.

min_free_gb.description: MinFreeGB is the disk admission floor (§5.3 check 4).

name.description: Name is the org-facing label (what the pools page renders).

org_id.description: OrgID is the declaring org — every read and write scopes by it.

packs.description:
Packs are the per-flavor packs (budgets + the concurrency lid +
the warm floor).

runner_forge.description:
RunnerForge + RunnerVersionPin are the pool's download-at-enlist
pin (the slice's runner downloads fresh at enlist, against this
pin — never a pre-baked image).

storage_pool.description: StoragePool names the host storage pool slices draw from.

virtualization.description:
Virtualization selects the backend class: incus-vm |
incus-container | docker.

budget_gb.description:
BudgetGB bounds the host's golden volumes total (§6.3 law 4): a
cache fill can never starve the packer. Positive when enabled.

min_free_gb.description:
MinFreeGB is the host free-space floor a cache volume create
additionally respects.

repo_scopes.description:
RepoScopes is the per-repo opt-in list ("owner/name" entries);
empty means org scopes only.

class_name.description:
ClassName names the VM class this flavor serves (the class the
catalog carries and the class jobs fit).

max_concurrent.description:
MaxConcurrent is the flavor lid: live slices of the flavor on the
host never exceed it.

min_idle.description:
MinIdle is the warm floor per flavor — a budget promise the
host-budget arithmetic reserves.

account.description:
Issue #3576 — Azure Blob (azblob) fields. Account is the storage
account name (the endpoint synthesizes from it) and Container is the
blob container; both are empty for every other provider. Bucket/region
semantics do not apply to azblob rows.

default_bucket.description: Optional: Default bucket for this connection

endpoint.description:
S3 endpoint (auto-filled based on provider, editable for "other")
AWS: https://s3.<region>.amazonaws.com
MinIO: https://<your-minio-host>:9000
Wasabi: https://s3.wasabisys.com
GCS: https://storage.googleapis.com
azblob: https://<account>.blob.core.windows.net (synthesized at create
when the request omits it — the column is not null, so the synthesized
value is stored).

linked_credential_id.description:
Issues #3576 (azblob) and #3874 (the S3 family) — link mode: when set,
the connection carries NO vault credentials of its own
(CredentialsEncryptedDataID stays nil) and authenticates at use time
through the linked CloudProviderCredential. azblob links an azure
credential's service principal (the ACR image-registry shape); the S3
family links an aws-shaped access-key pair (gcs links a gcp credential
only when it carries HMAC keys). Accepted pairs: aws/minio/wasabi/other
link an aws credential, gcs links a gcp credential, azblob links an
azure credential.

project_id.description:
Story 104.3: ProjectID is now nullable (*uint) so a row may be
org-scoped (ProjectID = nil) instead of project-scoped. The org-vs-
project distinction is one branch: `project_id IS NULL` = org-scoped.
AutoMigrate applies the NOT NULL → nullable change (dev-stage policy).

provider.description: aws, minio, wasabi, gcs, other, azblob

region.description:
Issue #3874 — the S3-family region. Key-mode rows also carry it inside
the sealed credential blob (that is where the probe read it before), but
link-mode rows store NO blob of their own, so the region the create
validated has nowhere else to live. Explore, the unified test-connection
check and the catalog capture read it here. Empty for azblob rows.

local_echo_enabled.description:
LocalEchoEnabled is the per-user terminal local-echo preference
(issue #774, Category AH). Default OFF everywhere: a user who never
toggled gets false, so console/SSH keystroke behavior is
byte-identical to the pre-#774 round-trip behavior until the user
opts in. GORM auto-migrate adds the column per house convention.

access_mode.description:
AccessMode (Epic 89 — BYOV VM Console) determines interactive-shell policy.
  byov     — user-owned VM (own_managed, user cloud key, multipass guest).
             End-user Console / SSH allowed (role-gated).
  platform — provisioned with a BMC system cloud credential
             (CloudProviderCredential.IsSystemOwned). End-user shell
             forbidden; future admin panel is a separate surface.

Default "byov" preserves existing UX for rows that predate this field
(GORM backfills the column default on AutoMigrate — dev-stage policy).

cluster_id.description:
Cluster association (optional - VM can be standalone or part of a cluster)
Note: Cascade deletion is handled at application level based on ClusterOrigin
- OriginCreated: VMs are deleted when cluster is deleted (if user opts in)
- OriginImported: VMs are never deleted automatically; only k8s is uninstalled

connection_type.description:
Polymorphic association for connection
connection_type examples: managed_ssh_connections, aws_key_pair, gcp_service_account

deletion_reason_code.description:
DeletionReasonCode is the machine-contract reason a VM removal landed in
cleanup_incomplete (issue #1454, AC3): one of the VMRemovalReason*
constants. NULL on every row not in cleanup_incomplete. The FE maps
codes → copy; unknown codes render status_reason (sanitized human
fallback detail), so the exact strings are a wire contract.

k3s_state.description:
K3SState is the guest-truth k3s lifecycle state of this VM's host
(story 124-1 AC6, epic-124): 'none' = no k3s installed on the guest;
'installed' = a successful SetupNode/uninstall-symmetric moment completed;
'unknown' = never observed (the default — rows predating the column and
guests outside cluster flows backfill nothing). Writers land ONLY at the
guest-state moments that exist today, both via WriteNodePhase (the
ADR-060 single-writer choke point): phase ready → installed,
phase removed → none. The 124.3 probe writer and the detach /
delete-keep writers arrive with their owning stories.

network_id.description: Network association (optional - VM can be part of a network)

org_id.description: Tenant scope (ADR-062): replaces the former owner-only UserID.

provider_vm_id.description: Provider-specific VM identifier (e.g., EC2 instance ID, GCP instance name, Azure VM name)

specs_status.description:
SpecsStatus is the EVIDENCE status of the CPU/RAM/disk spec columns
(story 124-2, D4): 'reported' = an agent metrics report carrying
cpu_count/memory_total_bytes/disk_total_bytes has been seen for this VM;
'unknown' = never observed (the default — no report, no inference). The
only writer after creation is the D4 projection in the metrics collector
(services.SpecProjector): create-time declared specs and the SSH display
migration are not evidence — specs_status stays 'unknown' for them. The
status is NEVER derived from the column values (never "0 means
unknown"). Consumers: cluster-create preflight (124.3) and the VM
pages' specs pill.

ssh_key_encrypted_data_id.description:
Encrypted SSH Key Storage (Polymorphic encrypted_data table)
References the EncryptedData table where the SSH private key is stored encrypted

ssh_public_key.description: SSH Access (for VMs where we provisioned SSH keys)

purpose.description:
Draft intent (story 124.17 AC7): 'cluster-create' when the wizard
created this network as a draft for the cluster named by DraftName.
Surfaces the Networks-page resume banner / "Prepared for a cluster"
chip without a per-row join-status call.

status_reason.description:
StatusReason carries the visible failure reason for the failed /
delete_failed states (#2359, #2362); empty on healthy rows. The FE
renders it under the status chip.

on_this_network.description:
OnThisNetwork badges selected-network members ("on N1" chip). False
for networkless candidates the wizard will PRE-JOIN.

rejection.description:
Rejection is the 124.3 server-computed preflight verdict for this VM —
the machine contract the picker cards render inline (disabled-with-
reason; the contamination card keys Adoptable). Nil/omitted = the VM
passes list-level classification; the create-time gate re-verifies with
a live probe (the list is a hint, the gate is the truth).

specs_unknown.description:
SpecsUnknown mirrors 124.2's specs contract: true while the VM's
health and specs are not yet agent-reported ("Waiting for agent data").

supported.description: Supported false = the platform cannot build this count today.

hosted.description:
Hosted is the hosted badge: every job this route reports is a
hosted-chain job.

provider_vm_id.description:
ProviderVMID is the floor VM's provider id while the job binds
one (the Epic 145.2 swap-scope note on the CP-API handler type
covers its exposure).

vm_seconds.description:
VMSeconds is the control-plane-computed metered amount;
DurationSeconds is the admitted-to-now-or-terminal wall clock.

org_id.description:
OrgID is the dispatch envelope's org (AAR.3 item 8): the
CP-asserted tenant identity the machine-side refusal gate keys
its different-org receipt check on. The pool set it from the
admitted job — never from the customer's metering tags.

provider_vm_id.description:
ProviderVMID is the machine's own dispatch address — an echo of
the credential-derived identity, never a caller-chosen value.

request.description:
Request is the request affordance (see
ReservationRequestAffordance): how an org asks for a reservation —
an admin conversation, never a purchase flow.

next_last.description: pass as last= on next page when Link present / truncated

active.description:
Active is the running-state gate: true only while the cluster is
operational (status provisioned). False = the panel renders honestly
dormant (stale keys may briefly outlive a transition; they are never
served as healthy).

cluster_status.description: ClusterStatus is the cluster's CURRENT status verbatim.

plane.description:
Plane is the measured operating plane (direct | mesh); empty when no
record exists.

node_status.description:
NodeStatus is the honesty state: measured | off_not_measured |
preparing_not_measured | address_diverged_not_measured | not_measured.

power_state.description: PowerState is the virtual_machines status (the power-state truth).

detail.description: Detail names the honest reason for a non-measured render.

rtt_ms.description:
RTTms is the connect round trip in milliseconds (0 unless Status is
measured or refused — the two classes a round trip backs).

status.description:
Status is the pair's HONESTY-ADJUSTED sample status: a stored sample
whose endpoint is currently stopped or diverged degrades to
LatMonPairNotMeasured at read time — RTTs are never served through a
node whose plane or power state no longer backs them.

detail.description: Detail names the probed size so the warning is actionable.

payload_size.description:
PayloadSize / PacketSize are the measured crossing sizes — the
verify_tailnet blocked record's exact shape (both 0: no DF packet of
the probed size crossed; small packets only).

port.description: Port is the first failing port of the set (0 for non-dial classes).

components.description:
Components groups mutually-reachable VM IDs so the UI can say "A, B,
C reach each other; D is isolated".

mtu_warnings.description:
MtuWarnings carries the mesh plane's pair-level large-packet
failures (issue #3378): WARNING entries, never verdict-changing. A
direct-plane response never carries them (the DF component is
mesh-plane only).

stale_note.description:
StaleNote is the ENGINE's honest escalation copy wired through when
Stale is true (review MED-2) — BE-owned, rendered verbatim; empty
(omitempty) on the fresh path.

components.description:
Components groups mutually-reachable VM IDs; CriticalVMIDs are the
members sitting on every path — the graph copy's data.

expired.description:
Expired true: a record exists but its validity lapsed — the
re-probe-offer state, distinct from never-measured.

measured.description: Measured true: a usable measurement fed the suggestion.

measured_at.description: MeasuredAt is when the feeding probe ran (present only when measured).

not_measured_reason.description: NotMeasuredReason is the honest why when Measured is false.

plane.description:
Plane is the selection's operating plane (Ruling 4): direct for a
networkless selection, mesh for a networked one.

network_measurement.description:
NetworkMeasurement is the story-144.4 honesty block (ADDITIVE — every
pre-existing key stays byte-identical).

blob.description:
Blob is the machine's sealed-delivery ciphertext, base64 — SD2's
moment-of-use redelivery riding the verify round-trip.

body.description: Body is the raw push body, base64.

delivery_id.description:
DeliveryID is the provider's own delivery id (the ledger's
correlation, surfaced in verdict audit rows).

event_type.description:
EventType is the raw event-type header (the machine verifies pings
too — the edge drops non-push events only after a verified verdict).

org_id.description: OrgID/TriggerID/AgentID are the tenancy and addressing triple.

provider.description:
Provider is the webhook provider slug (github|gitlab) — the machine
picks the verify recipe by it.

req_id.description: ReqID is the request's correlation id (the verdict queue's key).

signature.description:
Signature is the raw signature header value (X-Hub-Signature-256 or
X-Gitlab-Token — provider vocabulary preserved verbatim).

BearerAuth.description: Personal access token for SDK and CLI use: send `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Mint one with POST /me/tokens (needs a sudo window from POST /me/sudo).
BearerAuth.name: Authorization

EncryptionKeyAuth.description: Legacy (pre-ADR-067) security scheme name, kept only so existing @Security references stay valid. The vault unlock happens in the browser (issue #4027 — no server-side unlock endpoint or session token exists); org-scoped vault spend is authorized by one-time operation rentals minted at POST /orgs/:org_id/vault/rentals and pinned via the X-Vault-Rental-ID header.
EncryptionKeyAuth.name: X-Encryption-Key

OrgIDHeader.description: Organization ID for tenant list scoping (TenantListScope / Epic 85). Required with X-Project-Id on list/index routes.
OrgIDHeader.name: X-Org-ID

ProjectIdHeader.description: Project filter for tenant list routes: a numeric project id, or the case-sensitive sentinel `all` for every project the caller can access in X-Org-ID.
ProjectIdHeader.name: X-Project-Id
